findings.impact: In ClickyInkParser, Private Use Area char markers (BoldOn = '\ue001' = 57345, BoldOff = '\ue002' = 57346, HighlightOn = '\ue003' = 57347, HighlightOff = '\ue004' = 57348, LinkOn = '\ue005' = 57349, LinkOff = '\ue006' = 57350) were decompiled as integer literals inside interpolated replacement strings: BoldPattern.Replace(text, $"{57345}$1{57346}") and HighlightPattern.Replace(text, $"{57347}$1{57348}"). Because "57346" immediately follows "$1", .NET Regex.Replace interprets "$157346" as capture group 157346 (which does not exist) and outputs the literal string "57345$157346", completely erasing the user's bolded or highlighted words! Similarly, MarkingFirstLink outputs literal "57349label57350" instead of PUA characters. Verified dynamically by WsHiAuditRunner Test 6.
findings.remediation: Replace the integer literals in ClickyInkParser.EmphasisMarks (lines 1593-1594) and MarkingFirstLink (line 1619) with the char constants BoldOn/BoldOff ('\ue001'/'\ue002'), HighlightOn/HighlightOff ('\ue003'/'\ue004'), and LinkOn/LinkOff ('\ue005'/'\ue006').

findings.title: Unregistered Harness Drivers (pi-mac, h1-cloud, codex-cloud) and Hardcoded /usr/bin/tar in clicky-harness.exe Cause Immediate HTTP 500 Failures
findings.component: Agent Harness Sidecar & Runtime Selection (AgentHarnessRuntimes / clicky-harness.exe)
findings.description: Although clicky-harness.exe bundles @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent dead code in its Bun bundle, its entrypoint registers ONLY a single driver: Yf({drivers:{"h1-mac":{run:yf,steer:X_,cancel:R_}}}) (agents-harness-drivers.txt:186). findings.title: Unrestricted PowerShell (bash Tool) and Filesystem Write Access Outside Job Workspace Without Sandbox or User Approval
findings.component: Agent Harness Tool Execution & Safety Boundary
findings.description: In clicky-harness.exe ('h1-mac'), the local box tools ('bash', 'write', 'edit', 'read') execute directly with the user's full Windows account privileges. On Windows ($f = true), the 'bash' tool executes arbitrary Windows PowerShell commands with a 300-second timeout (bashTimeoutS: 300, agents-harness-drivers.txt:106, 133), and the 'write' and 'edit' tools resolve any absolute or relative path on disk without enforcing that the target path stays within A.workspace (agents-harness-bundle-excerpt.txt:123: We(n, a?.cwd || A)). There is no user confirmation/approval gate for shell execution or file writes outside the job workspace. Because agents routinely ingest untrusted external content via fetch_url, web_search, browser tabs, and Composio emails/messages, indirect prompt injection can execute arbitrary PowerShell commands or overwrite arbitrary user files.
reproductionSteps: Run Scenario 13 and Scenario 26 in tests/audit/ws-jk/test-agents-harness.ps1.

Observe that in Scenario 26, a model response invoking write with path='<tempStateDir>/outside-sandbox-proof.txt' (outside the job's workspace directory) succeeds without error or approval prompt and creates the file on disk.

findings.title: Complete C#-to-Backend DTO schema mismatch across GET /agent/integrations, POST /agent/integrations/:toolkit/connect, and POST /agent/composio/session breaks all agent integrations and Composio MCP session setup
findings.description: 1) AgentService.ListIntegrationsAsync() always returns 0 integrations because AgentIntegration.Parse() requires o['id'] (returns null if missing) and accounts[].connected_account_id, whereas agents.ts:843-876 returns toolkit, name, and accounts[].id. 2) AgentWorkerApi.ConnectIntegrationAsync() always throws AgentBackendException('HeyClicky received an invalid integration connect URL.') because it requires a non-empty redirect_url string, whereas agents.ts:896 returns connect_url: null. 3) AgentWorkerApi.ComposioSessionAsync() always returns (ComposioFetchKind.NoConnectedApps, Config: null, Error: null) because it checks enabled == true and proxy_url, whereas agents.ts:936-946 returns mcp_url and omits enabled. Root cause: Backend mock routes in src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:843-947 were written with guessed field names (toolkit/name, connect_url, mcp_url) instead of matching the C# parsers in AgentIntegration.cs and AgentWorkerApi.cs (id/display_name/status/toolkits/connected_account_id, redirect_url, enabled/proxy_url).

findings.category: API Contract / Caching & Model Selection Bug
findings.title: POST /agent/session-token returns expires_at as an ISO string instead of numeric Unix seconds and omits capabilities.developer_model_selection, permanently defeating AgentSessionTokenProvider caching (NeedsRefresh == true) and locking all turns to AgentHarnessModel.Standard
findings.description: 1) AgentSessionTokenProvider.NeedsRefresh is permanently true, causing redundant POST /agent/session-token HTTP requests on every tokens.GetAsync(ct) call. 2) tokens.AllowsDeveloperModelSelection is permanently false, forcing AgentService.cs:3672 to use AgentHarnessModel.Standard and ignoring ClickyAgentHarnessModel. 3) POST /agent/session-token returns two different UUIDs for session_token and token. Root cause: AgentWorkerApi.MintSessionTokenAsync (line 92) parses expires_at via TryGetValue<double> (Unix seconds); because agents.ts:916 sends an ISO-8601 string, it falls back to UtcNow + 15 minutes, which is immediately <= SessionTokenRefreshMargin (30 minutes at AgentRuntimeOptions.cs:24). In addition, agents.ts:911-922 omits capabilities: { developer_model_selection: true }.
reproductionSteps: Mint a token via POST /agent/session-token and inspect AgentSessionTokenProvider.NeedsRefresh (true immediately) and AllowsDeveloperModelSelection (false).
findings.observedResult: 1) AgentSessionTokenProvider.NeedsRefresh is permanently true, causing redundant POST /agent/session-token HTTP requests on every tokens.GetAsync(ct) call. 2) tokens.AllowsDeveloperModelSelection is permanently false, forcing AgentService.cs:3672 to use AgentHarnessModel.Standard and ignoring ClickyAgentHarnessModel. 3) POST /agent/session-token returns two different UUIDs for session_token and token.
findings.expectedResult: After MintSessionTokenAsync, NeedsRefresh is false for 30 minutes and AllowsDeveloperModelSelection is true.
findings.impact: Uncached HTTP round-trips to /agent/session-token on every turn preparation and inability to select non-Standard harness models (Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku).
findings.remediation: In src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:911-922, return a single token value, numeric expires_at: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600, and capabilities: { developer_model_selection: true }.

findings.title: Universal Pressable Control Lacks Keyboard Focus (IsTabStop) and Enter/Space Key Handling
findings.description: Pressable is the universal interactive control used for buttons, toggle switches, sidebar navigation rows, cards, and action chips across Settings, Notch, ArcDock, Home, Paywall, and Onboarding. Pressable inherits from Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Grid (Pressable.cs:18), where UIElement.IsTabStop defaults to false. Its constructor (Pressable.cs:181-242) only subscribes to PointerEntered, PointerExited, PointerPressed, PointerReleased, and PointerCaptureLost; it never sets IsTabStop = true, never displays a keyboard focus visual, and never handles KeyDown for VirtualKey.Enter or VirtualKey.Space. Across all 885 C# files in Kursor.App, IsTabStop = true is set in only 6 places.
reproductionSteps: Open Kursor Settings (or Intro/Tutorial/Paywall/Home window).
Press the Tab key repeatedly to navigate between sidebar items, toggle switches, and action buttons, and press Enter or Space to activate a control.
Inspect src/desktop/Kursor.App/HeyClicky.App.UI/Pressable.cs:181-242 and docs/audit/evidence/ws-jk/ui-static-analysis.json.

findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Severe accessibility failure (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard): keyboard-only and assistive-technology users cannot navigate or operate the Settings window, Onboarding flows, Paywall cards, or Notch/Dock actions via keyboard.

findings.title: Unbounded Synchronous `gunzipSync` in `gzipMiddleware` Enables Local/Cross-Origin Decompression Bomb DoS
findings.component: Backend HTTP Server / Gzip Decompression Middleware
findings.description: In `src/backend/src/middleware/gzip.ts:12-35`, whenever a request includes `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `gzipMiddleware` reads the entire request body via `await c.req.raw.arrayBuffer()` without checking `Content-Length` or streaming byte limits, and then calls `gunzipSync(compressedBuffer)` synchronously on the main Node.js event loop thread without passing a `maxOutputLength` option (`zlib.gunzipSync(buf, { maxOutputLength })`). A small 1–5 MB gzip bomb (expanding to multiple gigabytes of zeros) blocks the Node.js event loop and exhausts V8/Buffers memory, crashing the backend process.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `src/backend/src/middleware/gzip.ts:16-20`.
Observe `const compressedBuffer = Buffer.from(await c.req.raw.arrayBuffer()); const decompressed = gunzipSync(compressedBuffer);` with no input size cap and no `maxOutputLength` parameter.
See `poc3_gzipMiddleware` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/security-pocs.json`.
findings.observedResult: In `src/backend/src/middleware/gzip.ts:12-35`, whenever a request includes `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `gzipMiddleware` reads the entire request body via `await c.req.raw.arrayBuffer()` without checking `Content-Length` or streaming byte limits, and then calls `gunzipSync(compressedBuffer)` synchronously on the main Node.js event loop thread without passing a `maxOutputLength` option (`zlib.gunzipSync(buf, { maxOutputLength })`). A small 1–5 MB gzip bomb (expanding to multiple gigabytes of zeros) blocks the Node.js event loop and exhausts V8/Buffers memory, crashing the backend process.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Denial of service (event-loop freeze or OOM crash of the backend worker) triggerable by any local process or cross-origin browser page.
findings.remediation: Enforce a maximum compressed size check before buffering and pass `{ maxOutputLength: 20 * 1024 * 1024 }` to `zlib.gunzip` (async) inside `src/backend/src/middleware/gzip.ts:16-22`, returning HTTP `413` on `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE`.

findings.title: Open Redirect with Session Tokens on `GET /auth/v1/authorize` and Unconditional CSRF State Bypass in `SignInCallbackGuard`
findings.description: Two complementary flaws exist in the authentication callback chain: 1) In `src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:100-121`, `GET /auth/v1/authorize` reads `redirect_to` or `redirect_uri` from the query string, parses `new URL(redirectTo)`, and immediately appends `code`, `state`, `access_token`, and `refresh_token` before returning a `302` redirect to that URL without validating the scheme or host (allowing open redirects to `https://evil.attacker.example/...` with tokens in the URL). 2) In `src/desktop/Kursor.Core/HeyClicky.Core.Auth/SignInCallbackGuard.cs:60-65`, `SignInCallbackGuard.Evaluate` checks `if (isLocalSupabaseBackend) { return Verdict.AcceptLocalDevelopment; }` BEFORE checking whether `pendingState` exists (`line 67`) or matches `callbackState` (`line 75`). Because `IsLocalDevelopmentSupabaseUrl` is always `true` when `SupabaseUrl` points to `http://127.0.0.1:8787`, any external webpage that navigates to `heyclicky://auth-callback?access_token=<spoofed>&refresh_token=<spoofed>&referral_code=<code>` bypasses CSRF state validation, overwrites the user's persisted DPAPI auth session (`SupabaseAuthService.cs:223-241`), and triggers `ReferralCodeReceived` (`line 216`).
reproductionSteps: Request `GET http://127.0.0.1:8787/auth/v1/authorize?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.attacker.example%2Fcallback&state=csrf_test` with `redirect: manual`.

Observe the `302` `Location` header redirecting to `https://evil.attacker.example/callback?code=...&access_token=...&refresh_token=...` (`poc2_openRedirectTokenLeak` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/security-pocs.json`).
Inspect `SignInCallbackGuard.cs:60-65` and `SupabaseAuthService.cs:204-242` to verify that `isLocalSupabaseBackend == true` short-circuits all `pendingState`/`callbackState` checks.
findings.observedResult: Two complementary flaws exist in the authentication callback chain: 1) In `src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:100-121`, `GET /auth/v1/authorize` reads `redirect_to` or `redirect_uri` from the query string, parses `new URL(redirectTo)`, and immediately appends `code`, `state`, `access_token`, and `refresh_token` before returning a `302` redirect to that URL without validating the scheme or host (allowing open redirects to `https://evil.attacker.example/...` with tokens in the URL). 2) In `src/desktop/Kursor.Core/HeyClicky.Core.Auth/SignInCallbackGuard.cs:60-65`, `SignInCallbackGuard.Evaluate` checks `if (isLocalSupabaseBackend) { return Verdict.AcceptLocalDevelopment; }` BEFORE checking whether `pendingState` exists (`line 67`) or matches `callbackState` (`line 75`). Because `IsLocalDevelopmentSupabaseUrl` is always `true` when `SupabaseUrl` points to `http://127.0.0.1:8787`, any external webpage that navigates to `heyclicky://auth-callback?access_token=<spoofed>&refresh_token=<spoofed>&referral_code=<code>` bypasses CSRF state validation, overwrites the user's persisted DPAPI auth session (`SupabaseAuthService.cs:223-241`), and triggers `ReferralCodeReceived` (`line 216`).
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: An attacker webpage can either steal local session tokens via `/auth/v1/authorize?redirect_to=https://attacker/...` or force-overwrite the desktop client's auth session and referral code via a crafted `heyclicky://auth-callback?...` link.
findings.remediation: 1) Restrict `redirect_to` / `redirect_uri` in `src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:102-121` to `heyclicky:` or loopback (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`). 2) In `SignInCallbackGuard.cs:60-78`, verify `pendingState` == `callbackState` whenever `pendingState` is non-empty, or require an active sign-in flow before accepting `heyclicky://auth-callback` links.

findings.title: Vendor `HeyClickyApp` Binary Collision on Shared SingleInstance Mutex/MMF, `heyclicky://` Protocol Handler, Native Messaging Host, and Process Check in `start-kursor.ps1`
findings.description: Kursor's desktop build (`dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe`) retains the exact same executable name (`HeyClicky.exe`), single-instance mutex/MMF name (`Local\HeyClicky-<SID>-primary`), custom URI scheme (`heyclicky://`), Chrome Native Messaging host (`com.heyclicky.browser`), and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky` data folder as the original vendor installation (`C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe`). On the audit machine, `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` contains BOTH `HeyClicky` (`"C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe" --launched-at-login`) and `Kursor`. Because `start-kursor.ps1:113` checks `$existingDesktop = Get-Process -Name "HeyClicky" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` without verifying `$existingDesktop.Path`, when the vendor `HeyClickyApp` process is already running (verified live as PID 20080 from `C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe`), `start-kursor.ps1` skips launching `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` and logs `HeyClicky.exe already running`. Worse, even if `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` is launched manually, `SingleInstance.TryAcquire` sees `Local\HeyClicky-<SID>-primary-mutex` held by PID 20080, forwards its CLI arguments to the vendor binary over the named pipe (`HeyClicky-<SID>-20080-...`), and exits immediately (`Program.cs:35-38`)! Meanwhile, the running vendor binary overwrites `HKCU\Software\Classes\heyclicky\shell\open\command` and `BrowserHost\com.heyclicky.browser.json` with its own path and sends Sentry sessions (`sentry\Sentry\...\.session`) and device registration (`https://api.heyclicky.com/`) to the vendor cloud.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/env-and-surface-inventory.json` and `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/ipc-and-protocol-checks.json`.

Observe that `singleInstanceIpc.ownerPid` is `20080` (`C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe`), `HKCU\Software\Classes\heyclicky\shell\open\command` points to `"C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe" "%1"`, and `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` contains both `HeyClicky` and `Kursor`.
Inspect `start-kursor.ps1:113-124` to see that `Get-Process -Name "HeyClicky"` does not check whether the running process path matches `$DesktopExe` (`dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe`).

Because `start-kursor.ps1:113` checks `$existingDesktop = Get-Process -Name "HeyClicky" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` without verifying `$existingDesktop.Path`, when the vendor `HeyClickyApp` process is already running (verified live as PID 20080 from `C:\Users\ubaid\AppData\Local\HeyClickyApp\current\HeyClicky.exe`), `start-kursor.ps1` skips launching `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` and logs `HeyClicky.exe already running`. Worse, even if `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` is launched manually, `SingleInstance.TryAcquire` sees `Local\HeyClicky-<SID>-primary-mutex` held by PID 20080, forwards its CLI arguments to the vendor binary over the named pipe (`HeyClicky-<SID>-20080-...`), and exits immediately (`Program.cs:35-38`)! findings.remediation: 1) In `start-kursor.ps1:113-125`, filter `Get-Process -Name "HeyClicky"` by `.Path`—if any running `HeyClicky` process has `.Path -ne $DesktopExe`, stop that foreign process before launching `$DesktopExe`, and re-run `seed-local-auth.ps1` so the `heyclicky://` registry key points to `$DesktopExe`. 2) In `scripts/install-autostart.ps1`, remove any legacy `HKCU\...\Run\HeyClicky` value pointing to `HeyClickyApp`.

findings.category: Security / Privacy / Arbitrary Local File Upload Bypass
findings.title: ClickyBrowserBridge Turn-Wide uploadAnswers[task] Cache Allows Bait-and-Switch File & Site Exfiltration After Single Approval, Strips Directory Paths from Approval Cards, and BrowserUploads.IsSecretFileName Misses .db/.sqlite/.pfx/.kdbx Files
findings.description: Four compounding security flaws exist in the Chrome browser file-upload permission boundary: (1) Turn-wide approval cache ignores approved files and site: In ClickyBrowserBridge.UploadAnswerAsync (lines 1173-1193), once the user approves upload_approval for a benign file (e.g., files: ['notes.txt'] on trusted.com, or even an empty files array), uploadAnswers[task] = UploadApprovalAnswer.Allowed is cached keyed solely by task (thread + '/' + turn). Any subsequent upload or batch call in the same turn immediately receives UploadApprovalAnswer.Allowed (lines 1175-1180) without verifying whether the actual file paths (usersFiles) or target website (Site) match what the user approved—allowing a prompt-injected agent to bait-and-switch and exfiltrate up to 10 arbitrary files (100 MB) to an attacker tab. (2) Multi-site batch spoofing & path stripping: PrepareUploadsAsync (lines 1286-1287) strips directory paths via Path.GetFileName(f.Path) (so C:\Users\ubaid\Documents\payroll.csv displays only as 'payroll.csv') and passes only usersFiles[0].Site to the approval prompt even if later steps in a batch upload to a different domain. (3) Default-allow when customApprove is unset: PerformAsync (line 1088) evaluates bool flag5 = customApprove?.Invoke(title) ?? true;, defaulting browser access to true if customApprove is not wired. (4) Incomplete secret file blocklist: BrowserUploads.IsSecretFileName (BrowserUploads.cs:365-389) only blocks .env*, .pem, .key, .netrc, _netrc, .git-credentials, .npmrc, .pypirc, and .pgpass. It does NOT block .db, .sqlite, .db-wal (allowing upload of C:\dev\heyclicky-clone\src\backend\data\kursor.db, which stores unencrypted base64 screenshots, OneBrain memory, and session tokens!), .pfx, .p12, .kdbx, .rdp, .ovpn, or SSH private keys (id_rsa, id_ed25519) outside .ssh.
reproductionSteps:
1. Inspect ClickyBrowserBridge.cs lines 1173-1300 and BrowserUploads.cs lines 365-468.
2. Trace AskForUploadsUpFrontAsync with files: ['harmless.txt'] on tabId 1 (trusted.com): UploadAnswerAsync caches uploadAnswers[task] = UploadApprovalAnswer.Allowed.
3. Trace PrepareUploadsAsync on a subsequent upload call in the same turn with paths: ['C:\dev\heyclicky-clone\src\backend\data\kursor.db'] on tabId 2 (evil.com): UploadAnswerAsync returns the cached Allowed value without re-prompting, and BrowserUploads.ValidatedPaths allows kursor.db.
findings.observedResult: uploadAnswers[task] grants a turn-wide blanket approval for all files and sites; directory paths are stripped from approval prompts; customApprove defaults to true; and kursor.db / .pfx / .kdbx files pass ValidatedPaths.
findings.expectedResult: Upload approval must bind to the exact canonical resolved file paths and target origin (or re-prompt whenever an unapproved file path or different site is requested); approval cards must show full or parent-qualified paths; customApprove must default to false; and IsSecretFileName must block .db, .sqlite, .db-wal, .pfx, .p12, .kdbx, .rdp, .ovpn, id_rsa, and id_ed25519.
findings.impact: Four compounding security flaws exist in the Chrome browser file-upload permission boundary: (1) Turn-wide approval cache ignores approved files and site: In ClickyBrowserBridge.UploadAnswerAsync (lines 1173-1193), once the user approves upload_approval for a benign file (e.g., files: ['notes.txt'] on trusted.com, or even an empty files array), uploadAnswers[task] = UploadApprovalAnswer.Allowed is cached keyed solely by task (thread + '/' + turn). Any subsequent upload or batch call in the same turn immediately receives UploadApprovalAnswer.Allowed (lines 1175-1180) without verifying whether the actual file paths (usersFiles) or target website (Site) match what the user approved—allowing a prompt-injected agent to bait-and-switch and exfiltrate up to 10 arbitrary files (100 MB) to an attacker tab. (2) Multi-site batch spoofing & path stripping: PrepareUploadsAsync (lines 1286-1287) strips directory paths via Path.GetFileName(f.Path) (so C:\Users\ubaid\Documents\payroll.csv displays only as 'payroll.csv') and passes only usersFiles[0].Site to the approval prompt even if later steps in a batch upload to a different domain. (3) Default-allow when customApprove is unset: PerformAsync (line 1088) evaluates bool flag5 = customApprove?.Invoke(title) ?? true;, defaulting browser access to true if customApprove is not wired. (4) Incomplete secret file blocklist: BrowserUploads.IsSecretFileName (BrowserUploads.cs:365-389) only blocks .env*, .pem, .key, .netrc, _netrc, .git-credentials, .npmrc, .pypirc, and .pgpass. It does NOT block .db, .sqlite, .db-wal (allowing upload of C:\dev\heyclicky-clone\src\backend\data\kursor.db, which stores unencrypted base64 screenshots, OneBrain memory, and session tokens!), .pfx, .p12, .kdbx, .rdp, .ovpn, or SSH private keys (id_rsa, id_ed25519) outside .ssh.
findings.remediation: Key uploadAnswers by (task, normalizedSite, canonicalFilePathSet) in ClickyBrowserBridge.cs:1173-1299, verify every PlannedUpload.Site matches the approved site, change customApprove?.Invoke(title) ?? true to ?? false at line 1088, and expand BrowserUploads.IsSecretFileName to reject .db, .sqlite, .wal, .pfx, .p12, .kdbx, .rdp, .ovpn, id_rsa, and id_ed25519.

findings.title: README.md documents non-existent ONEBRAIN_MODEL (actual: KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL), .env.example omits KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL, and 6 env vars in .env.example are dead no-ops in backend code
findings.description:
Cross-checking `README.md`, `src/backend/.env.example`, and all `process.env.*` accesses in `src/backend/src/**/*.ts` (`docs/audit/evidence/ws-ab/docs-audit.json`) reveals three configuration mismatches:
1. **`ONEBRAIN_MODEL` vs `KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL`**: `README.md:84` tells users to set `ONEBRAIN_MODEL=google/gemini-2.5-flash`. However, `ONEBRAIN_MODEL` is never read anywhere in `src/backend/src/`! Instead, `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:598-599` and `959-960` read `process.env.KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL || process.env.OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL || "google/gemini-2.5-flash"`.
2. **`KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL` missing from `.env.example`**: `src/backend/.env.example` defines `OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL` (line 13) but omits `KURSOR_BRAIN_MODEL` (which takes precedence over `OPENROUTER_DEFAULT_MODEL` in `brain.ts` and is referenced in `docs/07-kursor-roadmap.md:76,144`).
3. **6 Dead Env Vars in `src/backend/.env.example`**: The following 6 variables in `src/backend/.env.example` are never read by any `.ts` file in `src/backend/src/`:

   - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (line 23)
   - `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` (line 55)
   - `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER` (line 61)
   - `BRAVE_API_KEY` (line 62)
   - `SERPER_API_KEY` (line 63)

findings.observedResult: Setting `ONEBRAIN_MODEL` (per `README.md:84`) or `KURSOR_DEV_BYPASS_AUTH=false` (per `.env.example:7`) has zero effect on backend behavior.
findings.expectedResult: `README.md`, `src/backend/.env.example`, and `src/backend/src/` must use identical environment variable names, and documented security/provider variables must either be wired into backend code or removed from `.env.example`.

findings.title: Moderate vulnerability in @hono/node-server@1.19.19 (GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f) and unverified Node.js engine version mismatch (>=24.0.0 vs v22+)
findings.description: Running `npm audit --json` in `src/backend/` reports a moderate-severity vulnerability (`GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f`, CVSS 5.3, CWE-174: Double decoding of percent-encoded paths in `@hono/node-server` `<2.1.3`, currently installed at `1.19.19` via `"@hono/node-server": "^1.19.11"`). Furthermore, `src/backend/package.json:25` specifies `"engines": { "node": ">=24.0.0" }` (and uses experimental `node:sqlite`), whereas `setup-kursor.ps1:29` and `README.md:127,140` tell users to install `Node.js v22+`, and `setup-kursor.ps1:27-32` only checks `if (-not $nodeVer)` without parsing or enforcing the major version number.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: `npm audit` reports 1 moderate vulnerability in `@hono/node-server@1.19.19`; `setup-kursor.ps1` accepts any Node version (even Node 16/18 where `node:sqlite` crashes at startup).
findings.expectedResult: `@hono/node-server` updated to `^2.1.3` (`0` vulnerabilities in `npm audit`), and `setup-kursor.ps1` enforcing the minimum Node version required by `node:sqlite`.
findings.impact: Running `npm audit --json` in `src/backend/` reports a moderate-severity vulnerability (`GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f`, CVSS 5.3, CWE-174: Double decoding of percent-encoded paths in `@hono/node-server` `<2.1.3`, currently installed at `1.19.19` via `"@hono/node-server": "^1.19.11"`). Furthermore, `src/backend/package.json:25` specifies `"engines": { "node": ">=24.0.0" }` (and uses experimental `node:sqlite`), whereas `setup-kursor.ps1:29` and `README.md:127,140` tell users to install `Node.js v22+`, and `setup-kursor.ps1:27-32` only checks `if (-not $nodeVer)` without parsing or enforcing the major version number.
findings.remediation: Upgrade `@hono/node-server` to `^2.1.3` in `src/backend/package.json`, and parse `[int](($nodeVer -replace '^v','').Split('.')[0]) -ge 22` (or `24`) in `setup-kursor.ps1`.

findings.title: Hardcoded developer filesystem paths in src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts (C:\Users\ubaid\...) and desktop C# files (C:\Users\niles\...)
findings.description: `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:7-8` hardcodes `const LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH = "C:\\Users\\ubaid\\AppData\\Local\\HeyClicky\\app-config.json";`. On any machine where the Windows username is not `ubaid`, `existsSync(LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH)` returns `false` and `/config` / `/app-config` falls back to `DEFAULT_APP_CONFIG_LINKS` pointing to `heyclicky.canny.io`, `reddit.com/r/heyclicky_`, and `heyclicky.com/changelog`. Additionally, `src/desktop/Kursor.App/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:14` hardcodes `C:\Users\niles\code\clicky-closed\windows\src\HeyClicky.App\` and `AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs:75` hardcodes `C:\Users\niles\code\clicky-closed\windows\src\HeyClicky.Agents\Harness\AgentHarnessRunnerRuntime.cs`.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: Hardcoded user profile paths (`C:\Users\ubaid\...` and `C:\Users\niles\...`) are embedded in backend and desktop source files.
findings.expectedResult: All paths must be resolved dynamically via environment variables (`process.env.LOCALAPPDATA`, `os.homedir()`, `AppContext.BaseDirectory`).
findings.impact: `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:7-8` hardcodes `const LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH = "C:\\Users\\ubaid\\AppData\\Local\\HeyClicky\\app-config.json";`. On any machine where the Windows username is not `ubaid`, `existsSync(LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH)` returns `false` and `/config` / `/app-config` falls back to `DEFAULT_APP_CONFIG_LINKS` pointing to `heyclicky.canny.io`, `reddit.com/r/heyclicky_`, and `heyclicky.com/changelog`. Additionally, `src/desktop/Kursor.App/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:14` hardcodes `C:\Users\niles\code\clicky-closed\windows\src\HeyClicky.App\` and `AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs:75` hardcodes `C:\Users\niles\code\clicky-closed\windows\src\HeyClicky.Agents\Harness\AgentHarnessRunnerRuntime.cs`.
findings.remediation: Replace `LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH` in `worker.ts:7-8` with `path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA || path.join(os.homedir(), 'AppData', 'Local'), 'HeyClicky', 'app-config.json')`, and remove `C:\Users\niles\...` from `AssemblyInfo.cs` and `AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs`.

findings.title: Split %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky vs %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor state between setup scripts and AppPaths.cs
findings.description: `setup-kursor.ps1:56-61` and `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:25-30,81-90` create and seed BOTH `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` with `endpoints.json`, `auth.localdev.bin`, and `auth.bin`. However, `src/desktop/Kursor.Contracts/HeyClicky/AppPaths.cs:12` resolves `Root` to `Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), "HeyClicky")` unless `KURSOR_DATA_DIR` or `HEYCLICKY_DATA_DIR` is set in the environment — which neither `start-kursor.ps1` nor `setup-kursor.ps1` sets. Consequently, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` is an orphaned decoy folder (containing stale files from earlier tests, including an unencrypted `session.json` and missing `auth.bin`), while all runtime state reads/writes happen in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky`.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: Both `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky` (18 files) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` (11 stale files) exist on disk, but the desktop app exclusively uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky`.
findings.expectedResult: A single canonical `%LOCALAPPDATA%` directory shared consistently by `AppPaths.cs`, `worker.ts`, `seed-local-auth.ps1`, and `setup-kursor.ps1`.
findings.impact: `setup-kursor.ps1:56-61` and `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:25-30,81-90` create and seed BOTH `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` with `endpoints.json`, `auth.localdev.bin`, and `auth.bin`. However, `src/desktop/Kursor.Contracts/HeyClicky/AppPaths.cs:12` resolves `Root` to `Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData), "HeyClicky")` unless `KURSOR_DATA_DIR` or `HEYCLICKY_DATA_DIR` is set in the environment — which neither `start-kursor.ps1` nor `setup-kursor.ps1` sets. Consequently, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` is an orphaned decoy folder (containing stale files from earlier tests, including an unencrypted `session.json` and missing `auth.bin`), while all runtime state reads/writes happen in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky`.
findings.remediation: Update `AppPaths.cs:12` to default to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` (with one-time migration from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky` if needed) or stop creating the unused `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kursor` directory in `setup-kursor.ps1` and `seed-local-auth.ps1`.

findings.title: Missing LICENSE / THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, unanchored [Rr]elease/ and [Dd]ebug/ rules in .gitignore, and non-resilient scripts/package-portable.ps1
findings.description:
1. **Missing license & attribution files**: The repository contains no `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, or `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` file in root.
2. **Unanchored `.gitignore` rules (`.gitignore:38-39`)**: `[Dd]ebug/` and `[Rr]elease/` match any directory named `Release` or `Debug` at any depth, while `release/` (lowercase, used by `scripts/package-portable.ps1:14`) is matched only by `[Rr]elease/`.
3. **`scripts/package-portable.ps1` fragility (`lines 25-56`)**: `Remove-Item $StageDir -Recurse -Force` and `Copy-Item -Path (Join-Path $RepoRoot "dist\kursor-desktop\*")` fail mid-execution if `HeyClicky.exe` or `clicky-harness.exe` is currently running and locking files in `dist/kursor-desktop/`, or if `dist/kursor-desktop/` has not been populated yet on a clean clone.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: No `LICENSE` file; unanchored `[Dd]ebug/` and `[Rr]elease/` patterns in `.gitignore`; `package-portable.ps1` does not check whether `dist/kursor-desktop/HeyClicky.exe` exists before packaging.
findings.expectedResult: Explicit `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, anchored `/release/` and `**/bin/[Rr]elease/` in `.gitignore`, and pre-flight validation in `package-portable.ps1`.

findings.category: Packaging Script Exit Code & Portable Archive Bloat
findings.title: scripts/package-portable.ps1 and scripts/build-dist.ps1 leave non-zero robocopy $LASTEXITCODE (1-7), and package-portable.ps1 bundles docs/audit/ and unusable build-dist.ps1 without src/desktop
findings.description:
1. Non-zero $LASTEXITCODE from robocopy: In scripts/package-portable.ps1:73 (`$null = robocopy $DistDir $DistStage /E ...`) and scripts/build-dist.ps1:46, robocopy sets $LASTEXITCODE to 1-3 on successful file copy. Because Compress-Archive is a PowerShell cmdlet (which does not reset $LASTEXITCODE), package-portable.ps1 exits with $LASTEXITCODE = 1 (or 3), causing automated callers or CI pipelines checking $LASTEXITCODE to treat a successful build/package as a failure.
2. Broken scripts & audit artifacts bundled in portable zip: scripts/package-portable.ps1:46 copies all of scripts/ (including build-dist.ps1 and overlay-and-launch.ps1) into the portable zip while omitting src/desktop/, so running scripts/build-dist.ps1 inside an extracted portable zip fails with 'Solution file not found'. Line 50 also copies the entire docs/ directory (including internal reverse-engineering specs and audit evidence) into the end-user portable zip.
reproductionSteps: Inspect scripts/package-portable.ps1 lines 45-52 and 73-84.
Verify that robocopy sets $LASTEXITCODE = 1 when copying files and neither script resets `global:LASTEXITCODE = 0` or checks `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ge 8) { throw ... }`.

findings.title: 4,712 'HeyClicky' and 19,632 'Clicky' references remain across desktop UI dialogs, tray window class, agent system prompts, and backend /app-config links
findings.description:
Codebase-wide regex scanning (`docs/audit/evidence/ws-ab/branding-scan.json`) found `4,712` occurrences of `HeyClicky` (across 2,095 desktop files) and `19,632` occurrences of `Clicky`. While primary window titles in `AppHost.cs` (`lines 525, 1986, 2005, 5810`) and tray menu labels in `TrayIcon.cs` (`lines 195-199`) were changed to `Kursor`, numerous user-visible surfaces still display `HeyClicky`:
- **Fatal crash & startup error dialogs**: `App.cs:111` (`"HeyClicky couldn't start... email hi@heyclicky.com"`, caption `"HeyClicky"`) and `SingleInstance.cs:345` (`"HeyClicky is already running... email hi@heyclicky.com"`).
- **Settings & Billing UI**: `BillingUi.cs:503` and `SettingsContent.cs:1205,2540` direct users to `hi@heyclicky.com`.
- **Tray Window Class & Plural Tooltip**: `TrayIcon.cs:232` registers Win32 window class `"HeyClickyTray"`, and `TrayTooltip.cs:25` formats `"${workingClickyNames.Count} Clickys working"`.
- **Agent System Instructions**: `CodexHomeManager.cs:74,75,88,91` injects instructions telling the AI agent to direct the user to `HeyClicky Settings -> Integrations`.
- **Backend `/config` & `/app-config` response**: `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:9-15` returns `https://heyclicky.canny.io/feature-requests`, `https://www.reddit.com/r/heyclicky_`, and `https://heyclicky.com/changelog?p=windows`.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: Crash dialogs, support emails, agent prompt injections, tray window class, and backend config links still expose `HeyClicky` and `hi@heyclicky.com`.

findings.title: SQLite Schema Lacks Secondary Indexes, Never Prunes Expired Sessions, and Bloats threads.messages_json With Raw Base64 Screenshots
findings.description: Inspection of `src/backend/src/db/index.ts` and `data/kursor.db` reveals three database scalability defects: (1) Zero secondary indexes (`CREATE INDEX`) exist on any of the 7 tables (`users`, `devices`, `memory`, `sessions`, `threads`, `notifications`, `proactive_cards`); `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` confirms full table scans (`SCAN sessions`, `SCAN notifications`) on `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE access_token = ?` and `SELECT * FROM notifications WHERE user_id = ?`. (2) Every `POST /auth/v1/token` and every `POST /brain/turn` with a new `session_id` inserts a row into `sessions` that is never deleted (`POST /brain/session-end` at `brain.ts:1284` only sets `expires_at = 0`). (3) `ensureSessionAndThread` (`brain.ts:172-187`) serializes the full `incomingThread` array—including raw base64-encoded screenshot images—into `threads.messages_json`, causing just 9 thread rows to bloat `kursor.db` to 4.0 MB and `kursor.db-wal` to 5.8 MB (~9.8 MB total).
reproductionSteps: Run `PRAGMA index_list(<table>)` across all 7 tables in `kursor.db`.
Run `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN DELETE FROM sessions WHERE access_token = ?` and `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM notifications WHERE user_id = ? AND dismissed = 0 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50`.
Check `sessions` row count before and after `POST /brain/turn` and `POST /brain/session-end`.

(2) Every `POST /auth/v1/token` and every `POST /brain/turn` with a new `session_id` inserts a row into `sessions` that is never deleted (`POST /brain/session-end` at `brain.ts:1284` only sets `expires_at = 0`). (3) `ensureSessionAndThread` (`brain.ts:172-187`) serializes the full `incomingThread` array—including raw base64-encoded screenshot images—into `threads.messages_json`, causing just 9 thread rows to bloat `kursor.db` to 4.0 MB and `kursor.db-wal` to 5.8 MB (~9.8 MB total).
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Progressive database file bloat (~1 MB per screenshot turn) and degrading query performance over time.
findings.remediation: Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` statements in `src/backend/src/db/index.ts`, strip `image_url` base64 blobs in `ensureSessionAndThread` (`src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:169`), and delete expired sessions (`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at > 0 AND expires_at < unixepoch()`).

findings.title: Proactive Jobs, Card Statuses, Turn Leases, Integrations, and Calendar Events Use Unbounded Volatile In-Memory State Lost on Restart
findings.description: Although `db/index.ts` defines a `proactive_cards` table in SQLite (`db/index.ts:86-97`), `src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts` never reads or writes `proactive_cards` in SQLite for job management. Instead, `proactiveJobs` (`agents.ts:47`), `proactiveCardStatuses` (`agents.ts:81`), `turnLeases` (`agents.ts:106`), `integrationsCatalog` (`agents.ts:127`), and `calendarEvents` (`agents.ts:163`) are kept purely in volatile JavaScript `Map` and `Array` objects in RAM, with no eviction/pruning of expired `turnLeases` or created `proactiveJobs`.

Restart the backend server process and query `GET /proactive/jobs`, `GET /agent/integrations`, and `GET /calendar/events`.

findings.title: Fragile Regex HTML Scraping in /search/web and HTML Tag Stripping Before Entity Decoding in decodeHtmlEntities
findings.description: `searchDuckDuckGoHtml` (`worker.ts:620-621`) scrapes `https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/` using a single attribute-order-dependent regex (`/<a[^>]+class="[^"]*result__a[^"]*"[^>]+href="([^"]+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/a>/gi`). When DuckDuckGo rate-limits or serves an anomaly/challenge page (which returns HTTP 200 with 0 regex matches), `/search/web` silently falls back to Wikipedia OpenSearch or returns a hardcoded dummy link to `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=...` with HTTP 200 (`worker.ts:755-764`). Furthermore, `decodeHtmlEntities` (`worker.ts:571-582`) strips `<[^>]+>` tags *before* decoding `<` and `>`, so HTML-encoded tags (`<script>` or `<system>`) in scraped snippets are decoded into raw tags and returned unescaped to LLM/agent consumers.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `decodeHtmlEntities` at `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:571-582`: `.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')` runs on line 573 before `.replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>')` on lines 576-577.
Inspect `searchDuckDuckGoHtml` fallback behavior at `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:744-768`.
findings.observedResult: `searchDuckDuckGoHtml` (`worker.ts:620-621`) scrapes `https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/` using a single attribute-order-dependent regex (`/<a[^>]+class="[^"]*result__a[^"]*"[^>]+href="([^"]+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/a>/gi`). When DuckDuckGo rate-limits or serves an anomaly/challenge page (which returns HTTP 200 with 0 regex matches), `/search/web` silently falls back to Wikipedia OpenSearch or returns a hardcoded dummy link to `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=...` with HTTP 200 (`worker.ts:755-764`). Furthermore, `decodeHtmlEntities` (`worker.ts:571-582`) strips `<[^>]+>` tags *before* decoding `<` and `>`, so HTML-encoded tags (`<script>` or `<system>`) in scraped snippets are decoded into raw tags and returned unescaped to LLM/agent consumers.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Brittle web search results and potential indirect prompt/markup injection into agent/OneBrain contexts consuming `/search/web` snippets.
findings.remediation: In `decodeHtmlEntities` (`worker.ts:571-582`), decode entities first and strip `<[^>]+>` tags last (or keep `<`/`>` escaped).

findings.title: nextSuggestionNumericId Resets to 101 on Backend Restart and Overwrites/Un-Dismisses Existing proactive_cards Rows in SQLite
findings.description: src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:85 initializes let nextSuggestionNumericId = 101; as an in-memory counter rather than seeding it from SELECT MAX(CAST(id AS INTEGER)) FROM proactive_cards. When createProactiveJob() runs (agents.ts:104-107, 156-175), it assigns IDs '101', '102', etc. and executes INSERT INTO proactive_cards (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET title = excluded.title, ..., dismissed = 0. Consequently, after every backend restart, the next proactive job creation reuses IDs 101, 102, ... and overwrites previously stored cards in SQLite, resetting dismissed = 0 on cards the user had already dismissed or resolved.
reproductionSteps: 1. Call POST /proactive/jobs (creates cards 101 and 102) and resolve/dismiss card 101 via POST /proactive/cards/resolve with {card_ids:['101'], resolution:'dismissed'}.
2. Restart the backend server (nextSuggestionNumericId resets to 101) and call POST /proactive/jobs again.
3. Query SELECT id, dismissed, payload_json FROM proactive_cards WHERE id = '101'.
findings.observedResult: Card '101' in SQLite is overwritten and its dismissed column is reset from 1 back to 0 (and status reset to 'presented').
findings.expectedResult: Initialize nextSuggestionNumericId from SELECT COALESCE(MAX(CAST(id AS INTEGER)), 100) + 1 FROM proactive_cards at startup (or use a SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT / UUID).
findings.impact: Previously dismissed or resolved proactive suggestion cards reappear as unread/active after a backend restart.
findings.remediation: Seed nextSuggestionNumericId from the SQLite proactive_cards table on startup in src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:85.

findings.title: GET /auth/v1/authorize and GET /auth/start Mint Access Tokens Without Inserting Session Rows Into SQLite sessions Table
findings.description: While POST /auth/v1/token (src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:198-207) inserts each minted access_token and refresh_token into the SQLite sessions table, GET /auth/v1/authorize (auth.ts:107-121) and GET /auth/start (auth.ts:131-175) call createLocalJwt(DEFAULT_USER_ID, DEFAULT_EMAIL) and return the minted access_token and refresh_token directly to the caller without inserting a row into SQLite sessions.
reproductionSteps: 1. Inspect src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts lines 100-175 vs lines 193-208.
2. Call GET /auth/start?format=json and check SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE access_token = <returned_token>.
findings.observedResult: 0 rows exist in SQLite sessions for tokens minted via GET /auth/v1/authorize or GET /auth/start.
findings.expectedResult: Every endpoint that mints an access_token and refresh_token must persist the session row in SQLite sessions so session validation, token refresh, and logout work consistently across all auth flows.
findings.impact: Inconsistent session state in SQLite; once AUD-C-004 is fixed to validate bearer tokens against the sessions table, tokens obtained via /auth/v1/authorize or /auth/start will be rejected as unknown sessions.
findings.remediation: Insert a sessions row in handleAuthorize (auth.ts:107) and handleAuthStart (auth.ts:131) using the same INSERT INTO sessions statement used in handleToken (auth.ts:198-207).

findings.title: analyzeScreenLayout Has 35.48% Strict Table Recall and 37.50% Strict Answer-Line Recall, Misses Solid/Dashed Lines (0% Recall), Falsely Detects Split Panes/Charts as Tables, and Places 640x480 Calm Cards Off-Screen
findings.description: Benchmarking `analyzeScreenLayout` across 66 corpus images (`tests/audit/ws-d/test-screen-layout.ts`) exposed multiple structural blind spots in its pixel heuristics: (1) Answer-line detection (`lines 405-481`) only counts short dark runs of `1..8px` (`if (inDot && runLen > 8) { inDot = false; dotCount = 0; }`) with `bestDots >= 50` and `span >= W * 0.35`, yielding **0% recall** on solid underline blanks (`29_lines_solid_underline_blanks`), dashed lines (`30_lines_dashed_10px_blanks`), wide-gap dots (`31`), short blanks (`32`), `<50` dots (`33`), light-gray dots (`35`), cream paper (`36`), and 2x DPI `2560x1440` dotted lines (`54`). Worse, when solid/dashed answer lines are missed (`numTables === 0 && numAnswerLines === 0`), `snapProgramToScreenLayout` Case A (`line 652`) replaces the LLM's valid `write(x, y, ...)` calls on the worksheet lines with a floating `receipt()` card! (2) Table detection (`lines 95-395`) requires `bg >= 160`, `>= 3` connecting vertical borders, `>= 4` horizontal lines, and `22 <= dy <= 115`, missing borderless tables (`08`), horizontal-only border tables (`09`), dark-mode tables (`12`, `13`), cream-shaded tables (`14`), skewed scans (`15`, `16`), tall rows `>115px` (`18`, `52`, `53`), and 2-row tables (`21`), while only keeping a single `bestGroup` (`tables.length <= 1` on multi-table screens `22`, `23`) and forcing `hasVisibleHeader = false` when `135 <= yMin < 175` (`17`). (3) Light IDE split panes (`43`) and bar charts with gridlines (`48`) trigger false-positive table detections (`2 FP`). (4) `candidateSpots` (`lines 486-490`) hardcode `1280x720` coordinates (`x: 860, y: 150, w: 390, h: 420`); on `640x480` (`55`, `56`), `x=860` is off-screen so the edge loop executes 0 iterations (`busy = 0`), selecting off-screen `(860, 150)` as the winning `calmCardSpot`!
reproductionSteps: Run `cd src/backend && npx tsx ../../tests/audit/ws-d/test-screen-layout.ts`.
Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-d/screen-layout-benchmark.json` for precision/recall summary and per-image results across all 66 corpus images.
findings.observedResult: Benchmarking `analyzeScreenLayout` across 66 corpus images (`tests/audit/ws-d/test-screen-layout.ts`) exposed multiple structural blind spots in its pixel heuristics: (1) Answer-line detection (`lines 405-481`) only counts short dark runs of `1..8px` (`if (inDot && runLen > 8) { inDot = false; dotCount = 0; }`) with `bestDots >= 50` and `span >= W * 0.35`, yielding **0% recall** on solid underline blanks (`29_lines_solid_underline_blanks`), dashed lines (`30_lines_dashed_10px_blanks`), wide-gap dots (`31`), short blanks (`32`), `<50` dots (`33`), light-gray dots (`35`), cream paper (`36`), and 2x DPI `2560x1440` dotted lines (`54`). Worse, when solid/dashed answer lines are missed (`numTables === 0 && numAnswerLines === 0`), `snapProgramToScreenLayout` Case A (`line 652`) replaces the LLM's valid `write(x, y, ...)` calls on the worksheet lines with a floating `receipt()` card! (2) Table detection (`lines 95-395`) requires `bg >= 160`, `>= 3` connecting vertical borders, `>= 4` horizontal lines, and `22 <= dy <= 115`, missing borderless tables (`08`), horizontal-only border tables (`09`), dark-mode tables (`12`, `13`), cream-shaded tables (`14`), skewed scans (`15`, `16`), tall rows `>115px` (`18`, `52`, `53`), and 2-row tables (`21`), while only keeping a single `bestGroup` (`tables.length <= 1` on multi-table screens `22`, `23`) and forcing `hasVisibleHeader = false` when `135 <= yMin < 175` (`17`). (3) Light IDE split panes (`43`) and bar charts with gridlines (`48`) trigger false-positive table detections (`2 FP`). (4) `candidateSpots` (`lines 486-490`) hardcode `1280x720` coordinates (`x: 860, y: 150, w: 390, h: 420`); on `640x480` (`55`, `56`), `x=860` is off-screen so the edge loop executes 0 iterations (`busy = 0`), selecting off-screen `(860, 150)` as the winning `calmCardSpot`!
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: On worksheets with solid or dashed blank lines, Kursor erases the LLM's inline `write()` answers and converts them into a single floating `receipt()` card; on `1080p`/`1440p` or dark-mode tables, snapping fails completely; on `<860px` windows, floating cards spawn off-screen.
findings.remediation: 1. Scale `candidateSpots`, row height limits (`22 * H/720 .. 115 * H/720`), and dot run lengths (`dotW <= 8 * W/1280`) by `(W / 1280, H / 720)` and clamp `calmCardSpot.x` to `<= W - spot.w - 16`. 2. Detect solid horizontal blank lines (isolated horizontal rules not connected to `>= 3` vertical table borders) and dashed lines (`runLen <= 16`) as `answerLines`. 3. Use relative contrast `Math.abs(bg - lum) >= 32` instead of `bg >= 160` so dark-mode tables are detected.

findings.title: snapProgramToScreenLayout Produces 'const w2 = ;' SyntaxError on Assigned write(), Matches Keywords Inside Comments/Strings, Hardcodes RISC/CISC Column Order, and Corrupts Coordinates on ViT Rescale & Combo Worksheets
findings.description: Adversarial testing of `snapProgramToScreenLayout` across 35 cases (`tests/audit/ws-d/test-screen-layout.ts`) confirmed 16 distinct failure modes in addition to AUD-D-003: (1) Case A (`lines 679-687`) replaces the 1st `write(...)` call with `receipt(...)` and replaces all subsequent `write(...)` calls with `""`. If the LLM assigned the result (`const w2 = write(...);`), replacing `write(...)` with `""` leaves `const w2 = ;` (`SyntaxError: Unexpected token` — confirmed in `SNAP-04` and `MATH-05`); (2) `hasTableMarks` (`line 646`) and `hasCardAlready` (`line 648`) run raw regexes across the entire code string without stripping comments or `say(...)` strings, so `// check(100, 200)` strips a valid `receipt()` card (`SNAP-31`) and `say("Look at paper(1)")` blocks Case A (`SNAP-32`); (3) `writeFullRegex` (`line 664`) and `point` regex (`line 736`) use `\{[^)]*\}` and `(?:,[^)]*)?\)`, failing when options contain `)` (e.g. `{ label: "a)" }` in `SNAP-06`) or leaving a dangling `});` `SyntaxError` (`SNAP-34`); (4) `lines 721-724` hardcode `risc` -> `answerCols[0].cx` and `cisc` -> `answerCols[1].cx`, swapping columns when CISC is Col 2 and RISC is Col 3 (`SNAP-11`); (5) `needsVitRescale` (`lines 756-776`) triggers whenever `avgX < minAnswerColX - 80` and multiplies Y by `720 / 565`, warping valid `1280x720` Y coordinates into the wrong row (`SNAP-15`); (6) `checksOnePerRow` (`lines 783-801`) overwrites bottom-up `check()` calls (`Row 4 -> Row 1`) into top-down order (`Row 1 -> Row 4`) whenever `bestDy > 20` (`SNAP-14`); (7) `lines 829-832` discard all `answerLines` above a table whenever `linesBelowTable.length > 0` and `check()` is used, moving `write()` calls for questions above the table down below the table (`SNAP-22`); (8) off-screen (`check(-500, 9999)` in `SNAP-09`) or non-table multiple-choice checkmarks (`SNAP-10`) and `point(..., "See Row 1")` (`SNAP-12`, `SNAP-13`) are hijacked into table cells.
reproductionSteps: Run `cd src/backend && npx tsx ../../tests/audit/ws-d/test-screen-layout.ts`.
Inspect all 19 failed adversarial cases in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-d/snap-program-adversarial.json` and `MATH-05` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-d/brain-prompt-matrix.json`.

findings.title: POST /brain/compact Never Persists to SQLite and Emits role='developer' Note Items That POST /brain/turn Drops; History Filter Drops Assistant Turns Without say() and Upstream Turn Path Never Emits computer_calls
findings.component: OneBrain Thread Compaction, History Filter & Session Lifecycle (brain.ts)
findings.description: End-to-end testing of `/brain/compact`, `/brain/session-end`, and multi-turn `/brain/turn` (`tests/audit/ws-d/test-brain-prompts.ts`) revealed 5 protocol and state bugs: (1) `POST /brain/compact` (`lines 1177-1251`) computes `note_item` and `keep_from_index` and returns them in JSON, but never updates `threads.messages_json` in SQLite; (2) `POST /brain/compact` sets `note_item.role = "developer"` (`line 1224`), while `POST /brain/turn` (`line 517`) filters `thread` with `item.type === "message" && (item.role === "user" || item.role === "assistant")`, silently dropping the compacted `note_item` on every subsequent turn; (3) `POST /brain/turn` (`lines 538-550`) strips assistant history by extracting `say(...)` regex matches and only pushes an assistant message `if (sayMatches.length > 0)`, completely dropping any assistant turn that only drew visual marks without `say(...)`, as well as any user message that omits `type: "message"` (`line 516`); (4) `tryCallUpstreamLlm` (`lines 397-408, 1039-1056`) never populates or returns `computerCalls`, so `computer_calls` SSE events (`lines 1083-1088`) are only ever emitted in `buildLocalFallbackProgram` when `body.force_computer_call` is passed; (5) `POST /brain/compact` (`line 1181`) and `POST /brain/session-end` (`line 1261`) swallow malformed JSON bodies and return `HTTP 200`, and `/brain/session-end` performs zero memory extraction/consolidation into `user_memory`.
reproductionSteps: Run `cd src/backend && npx tsx ../../tests/audit/ws-d/test-brain-prompts.ts`.

Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-d/brain-prompt-matrix.json` under `endpointContracts.compactEndpointAudit`, `endpointContracts.historyFilteringAudit`, `endpointContracts.invalidJsonHandling`, and `endpointContracts.sessionEndAudit`.
findings.observedResult: End-to-end testing of `/brain/compact`, `/brain/session-end`, and multi-turn `/brain/turn` (`tests/audit/ws-d/test-brain-prompts.ts`) revealed 5 protocol and state bugs: (1) `POST /brain/compact` (`lines 1177-1251`) computes `note_item` and `keep_from_index` and returns them in JSON, but never updates `threads.messages_json` in SQLite; (2) `POST /brain/compact` sets `note_item.role = "developer"` (`line 1224`), while `POST /brain/turn` (`line 517`) filters `thread` with `item.type === "message" && (item.role === "user" || item.role === "assistant")`, silently dropping the compacted `note_item` on every subsequent turn; (3) `POST /brain/turn` (`lines 538-550`) strips assistant history by extracting `say(...)` regex matches and only pushes an assistant message `if (sayMatches.length > 0)`, completely dropping any assistant turn that only drew visual marks without `say(...)`, as well as any user message that omits `type: "message"` (`line 516`); (4) `tryCallUpstreamLlm` (`lines 397-408, 1039-1056`) never populates or returns `computerCalls`, so `computer_calls` SSE events (`lines 1083-1088`) are only ever emitted in `buildLocalFallbackProgram` when `body.force_computer_call` is passed; (5) `POST /brain/compact` (`line 1181`) and `POST /brain/session-end` (`line 1261`) swallow malformed JSON bodies and return `HTTP 200`, and `/brain/session-end` performs zero memory extraction/consolidation into `user_memory`.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Thread compaction is non-functional in SQLite and its summary `note_item` is discarded on the very next turn; multi-turn conversations lose assistant turns without `say()`, resulting in adjacent `user` messages.
findings.remediation: 1. In `POST /brain/compact` (`brain.ts:1239`), persist `[noteItem, ...thread.slice(keepFromIndex)]` to `threads.messages_json` when `session_id` exists in SQLite. 2. In `tryCallUpstreamLlm` (`brain.ts:516-554`), include `item.role === "developer"` (mapped to `role: "system"` or `"user"` for providers that reject `developer`), allow history items where `item.type` is omitted, and fall back to a placeholder summary (`step(1); // previous drawing`) when an assistant turn has no `say()` match. 3. Map upstream `computer` / GUI action tool calls into `computerCalls` so `computer_calls` SSE events are emitted on live LLM turns.

findings.title: BrainReplyAccumulator Compares Unstripped lastReportedCode.Length Against URL-Stripped text3.Length in Finish(), Dropping Final Code Updates When Links Are Stripped
findings.description: During SSE streaming (`ReportCodeIfItGrew` at `BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:243-249`), `lastReportedCode` is assigned the raw `ProgramText.ProgramCode(rawText, isComplete: false)` *before* `ProgramText.WithoutLinks(text)` strips URLs/markdown links, so `lastReportedCode.Length` includes the length of any stripped URLs. When the stream finishes (`Finish()` at `lines 229-235`), `text3` is computed *after* `ProgramText.WithoutLinks(...)` and compared via `if (text3.Length > 0 && text3.Length > lastReportedCode.Length)`. If `WithoutLinks` stripped a URL or markdown link whose byte length exceeds the final streamed chunk length, `text3.Length <= lastReportedCode.Length`, and `Finish()` silently skips `onCodeUpdate?.Invoke(text3)`, leaving the live drawing engine with an incomplete program.
reproductionSteps: Compare `BrainReplyAccumulator.ReportCodeIfItGrew` (`lines 243-249`) with `BrainReplyAccumulator.Finish` (`lines 229-235`).
Trace a streamed program containing a URL outside strings (e.g., a trailing comment `// https://example.com/very/long/path`) where the final chunk is `< 35` chars.
findings.observedResult: During SSE streaming (`ReportCodeIfItGrew` at `BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:243-249`), `lastReportedCode` is assigned the raw `ProgramText.ProgramCode(rawText, isComplete: false)` *before* `ProgramText.WithoutLinks(text)` strips URLs/markdown links, so `lastReportedCode.Length` includes the length of any stripped URLs. When the stream finishes (`Finish()` at `lines 229-235`), `text3` is computed *after* `ProgramText.WithoutLinks(...)` and compared via `if (text3.Length > 0 && text3.Length > lastReportedCode.Length)`. If `WithoutLinks` stripped a URL or markdown link whose byte length exceeds the final streamed chunk length, `text3.Length <= lastReportedCode.Length`, and `Finish()` silently skips `onCodeUpdate?.Invoke(text3)`, leaving the live drawing engine with an incomplete program.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Streaming programs from which `WithoutLinks` strips URLs can drop their final `onCodeUpdate` invocation at stream completion.
findings.remediation: In `BrainReplyAccumulator.ReportCodeIfItGrew` (`line 246`), set `string stripped = ProgramText.WithoutLinks(text);` and compare/store `stripped` in `lastReportedCode`, and in `Finish()` (`line 231`) check `if (text3.Length > 0 && text3 != lastReportedCode)`.

findings.title: POST /brain/turn Always Wraps Output in Fenced ```js Blocks, Defeating BrainReplyAccumulator.SpeechOnly Mode
findings.component: OneBrain SpeechOnly Mode Contract (brain.ts vs BrainReplyAccumulator.cs)
findings.description: `BrainReplyAccumulator` (`BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:37, 58, 215-226`) supports a `SpeechOnly` mode where `Finish()` checks `if (SpeechOnly && !text.Contains("```", StringComparison.Ordinal))` to populate `Reply.SpokenSentence` and wrap plain spoken prose into `SayLine(...)`. However, `POST /brain/turn` (`brain.ts:249, 682`) unconditionally wraps every upstream and fallback response in ```` ```js ... ``` ```` fences regardless of request flags. Consequently, `!text.Contains("```")` is always `false` and `Reply.SpokenSentence` is never populated.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `BrainReplyAccumulator.Finish()` at `BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:215-226`.
Inspect `tryCallUpstreamLlm` (`brain.ts:682`) and `buildLocalFallbackProgram` (`brain.ts:249`).
findings.observedResult: `BrainReplyAccumulator` (`BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:37, 58, 215-226`) supports a `SpeechOnly` mode where `Finish()` checks `if (SpeechOnly && !text.Contains("```", StringComparison.Ordinal))` to populate `Reply.SpokenSentence` and wrap plain spoken prose into `SayLine(...)`. findings.title: Dictating While Focused on a Password Field (IsSecure) Archives Plaintext to Disk and Copies It to Non-Transient Clipboard (Exposed to Windows Clipboard History & Cloud Sync)
findings.component: Desktop Dictation Privacy & Password Field Protection (DictationController / TextInsertion)
findings.description:
When the user's cursor is inside a password field (focus.IsSecure == true, detected via UIA IsPasswordProperty or Edit ES_PASSWORD style in DictationTextTarget.cs:635-667):
1. DictationTextTarget.TryInsertCoreAsync (line 454) refuses to auto-paste and returns DictationInsertOutcome.RefusedUnsafeTarget.
2. However, BEFORE checking focus.IsSecure or calling textTarget.Insert, DictationController.DeliverAsync (line 612) unconditionally calls ArchiveTranscript(trimmed, rawBeforeCleanup, source, lang, focus.AppName, focus.SiteHost), writing the plaintext transcript to %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl!
3. Next, in the DictationInsertOutcome.RefusedUnsafeTarget handler (lines 667-688), DictationController calls CopyTranscriptToClipboardAsync(trimmed) (line 958), which calls TextInsertion.CopyTextAsync(text) (TextInsertion.cs:176-179). CopyTextAsync passes markTransient: false to SetClipboardTextWithRetry (line 178) — which skips setting ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing, CanIncludeInClipboardHistory = 0, and CanUploadToCloudClipboard = 0 (lines 270-275)! Thus, text dictated while focused on a password field is persisted in plaintext JSONL logs on disk AND synced to Windows Clipboard History (Win+V) and Microsoft Cloud Clipboard.
reproductionSteps: Focus a password input field (where focus.IsSecure == true).
Trigger dictation and speak a passphrase or sensitive string.
Inspect DictationController.DeliverAsync (lines 612 and 667-688) and TextInsertion.CopyTextAsync (lines 176-179).
findings.observedResult:
When the user's cursor is inside a password field (focus.IsSecure == true, detected via UIA IsPasswordProperty or Edit ES_PASSWORD style in DictationTextTarget.cs:635-667):
1. DictationTextTarget.TryInsertCoreAsync (line 454) refuses to auto-paste and returns DictationInsertOutcome.RefusedUnsafeTarget.
2. However, BEFORE checking focus.IsSecure or calling textTarget.Insert, DictationController.DeliverAsync (line 612) unconditionally calls ArchiveTranscript(trimmed, rawBeforeCleanup, source, lang, focus.AppName, focus.SiteHost), writing the plaintext transcript to %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl!
3. Next, in the DictationInsertOutcome.RefusedUnsafeTarget handler (lines 667-688), DictationController calls CopyTranscriptToClipboardAsync(trimmed) (line 958), which calls TextInsertion.CopyTextAsync(text) (TextInsertion.cs:176-179). CopyTextAsync passes markTransient: false to SetClipboardTextWithRetry (line 178) — which skips setting ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing, CanIncludeInClipboardHistory = 0, and CanUploadToCloudClipboard = 0 (lines 270-275)! Thus, text dictated while focused on a password field is persisted in plaintext JSONL logs on disk AND synced to Windows Clipboard History (Win+V) and Microsoft Cloud Clipboard.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Sensitive credentials or passphrases dictated while a password box is focused are permanently logged in plaintext under %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\ and leaked into Windows Clipboard History / Cloud Clipboard.
findings.remediation: 1. In DictationController.DeliverAsync, guard ArchiveTranscript with if (!focus.IsSecure). 2. In TextInsertion.CopyTextAsync (or when copying on RefusedUnsafeTarget), pass markTransient: true so clipboard history and cloud sync exclude the content.

findings.title: localCleanupHeuristic Corrupts URLs, Code/CLI Identifiers, Emoji Endings, and Returns Raw Filler Words When Utterance Is 100% Disfluencies
findings.description:
In localCleanupHeuristic (src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:459-480), four edge-case bugs corrupt dictated text whenever offline/heuristic cleanup runs:
1. Pure-filler utterances return raw fillers instead of empty string: After stripping fillers ('um', 'uh', 'ah', 'er', 'erm'), line 469 checks if (!cleaned) return raw.trim(). If the user only said 'um' or 'uh um erm', cleaned becomes '', and line 469 returns 'um' or 'uh um erm' instead of ''!
2. Unconditional first-character capitalization (line 472): cleaned.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cleaned.slice(1) mutates lowercase URLs ('https://api.example.com/v1/users' -> 'Https://api.example.com/v1/users'), camelCase identifiers ('useTriggerChatTransport' -> 'UseTriggerChatTransport'), and CLI commands ('kubectl get pods -n kube-system' -> 'Kubectl get pods -n kube-system').
3. Unconditional trailing period (lines 475-477): if (!/[.!?]$/.test(cleaned)) cleaned += '.' appends a period to URLs ('Https://api.example.com/v1/users.'), code statements ending in ';' or ')' ('const x = 42;.' / 'console.log(foo).'), and utterances ending with emojis ('Thank you 😊.').
4. Repeated punctuation produced by removing mid-clause fillers: Removing 'um' from 'Hello, um, how are you?' leaves 'Hello, , how are you?' with double commas.
reproductionSteps: Call localCleanupHeuristic('um') or POST /v2/dictation/cleanup with provider keys disabled and raw_text: 'um'. Observe it returns 'um'.
Call localCleanupHeuristic('https://api.example.com/v1/users'). Observe it returns 'Https://api.example.com/v1/users.'.
Call localCleanupHeuristic('git commit -m "fix bug"'). Observe it returns 'Git commit -m "fix bug".'.
Call localCleanupHeuristic('Hello, um, how are you?'). Observe it returns 'Hello, , how are you?'.
findings.observedResult:
In localCleanupHeuristic (src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:459-480), four edge-case bugs corrupt dictated text whenever offline/heuristic cleanup runs:
1. Pure-filler utterances return raw fillers instead of empty string: After stripping fillers ('um', 'uh', 'ah', 'er', 'erm'), line 469 checks if (!cleaned) return raw.trim(). If the user only said 'um' or 'uh um erm', cleaned becomes '', and line 469 returns 'um' or 'uh um erm' instead of ''!
2. Unconditional first-character capitalization (line 472): cleaned.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cleaned.slice(1) mutates lowercase URLs ('https://api.example.com/v1/users' -> 'Https://api.example.com/v1/users'), camelCase identifiers ('useTriggerChatTransport' -> 'UseTriggerChatTransport'), and CLI commands ('kubectl get pods -n kube-system' -> 'Kubectl get pods -n kube-system').
3. Unconditional trailing period (lines 475-477): if (!/[.!?]$/.test(cleaned)) cleaned += '.' appends a period to URLs ('Https://api.example.com/v1/users.'), code statements ending in ';' or ')' ('const x = 42;.' / 'console.log(foo).'), and utterances ending with emojis ('Thank you 😊.').
4. Repeated punctuation produced by removing mid-clause fillers: Removing 'um' from 'Hello, um, how are you?' leaves 'Hello, , how are you?' with double commas.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Offline/fallback dictation cleanup breaks pasted URLs, shell commands, code identifiers, and injects 'Um.' when the user only clears their throat or hesitates.
findings.remediation: In localCleanupHeuristic (voice.ts:459-480): return '' when cleaned is empty after filler removal; collapse /(,\s*){2,}/g to ', '; and guard first-letter capitalization and trailing period insertion against URLs (/^https?:\/\//i), code/CLI tokens, and emoji endings.

findings.title: ShortcutMonitor Lacks Non-Modifier Chord Cancellation for PushToTalk (Ctrl+Alt), Leaving Microphone Hot During IDE/Windows Shortcuts and Ctrl+LeftAlt International Keystrokes
findings.component: Win32 Low-Level Keyboard Hook & Hotkey State Machine (ShortcutMonitor)
findings.description:
Kursor's default PushToTalk hotkey is Ctrl+Alt (HotkeyBinding.DefaultPushToTalk) and default Dictation hotkey is Ctrl+Win (HotkeyBinding.DefaultDictation). In ShortcutMonitor.ProcessKeyboardEvent:
1. When Ctrl+Win (Dictation) is held and the user presses any non-modifier key (e.g. Ctrl+Win+Left/Right to switch virtual desktops), lines 429-434 set dictationChordCanceledByOtherKey = true, isDictationHeld = false, and enqueue ShortcutAction.DictationCancel.
2. However, for PushToTalk (Ctrl+Alt), there is NO equivalent chord-cancellation guard! When the user holds Ctrl+Alt to press an IDE shortcut (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+L to format code, Ctrl+Alt+T, Ctrl+Alt+Del) or types an international character using Ctrl+LeftAlt+<Key> (which Windows treats as equivalent to AltGr on international keyboards, since SuppressAltGrRightAlt at line 646 only suppresses VK_RMENU), ShortcutMonitor fires ShortcutAction.PushToTalkDown as soon as Ctrl+Alt are depressed and NEVER cancels PushToTalk when the non-modifier key is pressed!
reproductionSteps: Configure PushToTalk as default Ctrl+Alt.
Press Ctrl+Alt+L (or any Ctrl+LeftAlt+<key> shortcut in an IDE or international layout).
Inspect ShortcutMonitor.cs:416-438 and observe that only isDictationHeld is canceled on non-modifier keydown; isPushToTalkHeld stays true.
findings.observedResult:
Kursor's default PushToTalk hotkey is Ctrl+Alt (HotkeyBinding.DefaultPushToTalk) and default Dictation hotkey is Ctrl+Win (HotkeyBinding.DefaultDictation). In ShortcutMonitor.ProcessKeyboardEvent:
1. When Ctrl+Win (Dictation) is held and the user presses any non-modifier key (e.g. Ctrl+Win+Left/Right to switch virtual desktops), lines 429-434 set dictationChordCanceledByOtherKey = true, isDictationHeld = false, and enqueue ShortcutAction.DictationCancel.
2. However, for PushToTalk (Ctrl+Alt), there is NO equivalent chord-cancellation guard! When the user holds Ctrl+Alt to press an IDE shortcut (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+L to format code, Ctrl+Alt+T, Ctrl+Alt+Del) or types an international character using Ctrl+LeftAlt+<Key> (which Windows treats as equivalent to AltGr on international keyboards, since SuppressAltGrRightAlt at line 646 only suppresses VK_RMENU), ShortcutMonitor fires ShortcutAction.PushToTalkDown as soon as Ctrl+Alt are depressed and NEVER cancels PushToTalk when the non-modifier key is pressed!
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Every Ctrl+Alt+<Key> shortcut in IDEs/Windows (and Ctrl+LeftAlt+<Key> international character entry) inadvertently activates Clicky's Push-To-Talk voice session.
findings.remediation: In ShortcutMonitor.ProcessKeyboardEvent (lines 429-437), add pttChordCanceledByOtherKey and enqueue ShortcutAction.PushToTalkUp (or a dedicated PushToTalkCancel action) whenever a non-modifier key is pressed during a modifier-only PushToTalk hold.

findings.title: Warm PowerShell TTS Daemon (warmSynthProc) Is Spawned at Module Import Time with No Process Exit or Signal Cleanup Handlers
findings.component: Backend TTS ('Mouth') / Warm SAPI Worker Lifecycle
findings.description: In src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts (lines 314-320), ensureWarmSynthWorker() is executed eagerly at module import time on Windows, spawning a persistent child process (`powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command ...`) stored in warmSynthProc. There are zero process.on('exit'), process.on('SIGINT'), or process.on('SIGTERM') handlers anywhere in the backend to close warmSynthProc.stdin or kill warmSynthProc when the Node server shuts down or restarts under a watcher (e.g. tsx watch). Additionally, if warmSynthProc crashes while warmSynthQueue has in-flight or waiting items, proc.on('exit') (lines 279-283) sets warmSynthProc = null and warmSynthBusy = false WITHOUT resolving the pending Promises in warmSynthQueue, forcing callers to hang until their 7000ms timer expires.
reproductionSteps: Import src/backend/src/index.ts on Windows and verify a child powershell.exe process is immediately spawned by voice.ts:316.
Inspect voice.ts:232-285 for process exit/signal cleanup handlers (none exist) and inspect proc.on('exit') (lines 279-283) when warmSynthQueue is non-empty.
findings.observedResult: In src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts (lines 314-320), ensureWarmSynthWorker() is executed eagerly at module import time on Windows, spawning a persistent child process (`powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command ...`) stored in warmSynthProc. There are zero process.on('exit'), process.on('SIGINT'), or process.on('SIGTERM') handlers anywhere in the backend to close warmSynthProc.stdin or kill warmSynthProc when the Node server shuts down or restarts under a watcher (e.g. tsx watch). Additionally, if warmSynthProc crashes while warmSynthQueue has in-flight or waiting items, proc.on('exit') (lines 279-283) sets warmSynthProc = null and warmSynthBusy = false WITHOUT resolving the pending Promises in warmSynthQueue, forcing callers to hang until their 7000ms timer expires.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Abrupt server restarts or dev watcher reloads can leave orphaned powershell.exe processes, and worker crashes stall queued TTS callers for the full 7000ms timeout.
findings.remediation: Add process exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup hooks for warmSynthProc and drain/resolve pending warmSynthQueue entries inside proc.on('exit').

findings.title: DictationCorrectionDetector Auto-Learns Ordinary Sentence-Initial Capitalized Words and Sensitive Tokens Due to char.IsUpper(word[0]) and NormalizedSimilarity >= 0.3
findings.description:
After dictation pastes text into a target control, DictationController.SchedulePostInsertObservationAsync (lines 727-810) polls the control at 2.5s, 6s, and 12s and runs DictationCorrectionDetector.DetectSingleWordCorrection(insertedText, currentText, insertedText) to auto-learn vocabulary into settings.json (dictation_custom_words). Two flaws cause high false-positive rates and privacy leakage:
1. Over-permissive distinctiveness check (line 82): IsDistinctiveLearnableWord returns true for ANY word of length 2..40 where char.IsUpper(word[0]) is true! Because every dictated sentence begins with a capital letter, ANY single-word edit to the first word of a sentence (or any Title-cased word) passes IsDistinctiveLearnableWord unless it happens to be in the tiny 68-word CommonWords set.
2. Ultra-low similarity threshold (line 56): NormalizedSimilarity(beforeWord, afterWord) >= 0.3 requires only 30% character overlap (up to 70% Levenshtein distance!). Consequently, ordinary wording edits at the start of a sentence — such as changing 'Can' -> 'May' (similarity 0.333), 'The' -> 'She' (0.667), 'Good' -> 'Food' (0.75), 'Test' -> 'Best' (0.75), or 'Send' -> 'Read' (0.50) — are falsely classified as phonetic STT corrections and permanently added to dictation_custom_words in settings.json and sent to cloud STT/LLM providers as keyterms!
3. Secret/token leakage: Any word containing digits, underscores, or internal capitals (e.g. API keys like sk_live_987654321 or camelCase internal passwords) edited into the text within 12s passes IsDistinctiveLearnableWord and is persisted in plaintext in settings.json and transmitted in every subsequent /v2/dictation/gemini-token, /v2/dictation/transcribe, and /v2/dictation/cleanup request.
reproductionSteps: Run DictationCorrectionDetector.DetectSingleWordCorrection('Can you review the PR?', 'May you review the PR?', 'Can you review the PR?').
Observe that 'Can' -> 'May' has Levenshtein distance 2, length 3, NormalizedSimilarity = 0.333 >= 0.3, and 'May' has char.IsUpper('M') == true and is not in CommonWords.
Observe that DetectSingleWordCorrection returns 'May' as a learned custom vocabulary word.
