findings.remediation: In DictationCorrectionDetector.cs: pass word position to IsDistinctiveLearnableWord so index-0 capitalization alone does not qualify; raise NormalizedSimilarity threshold to 0.60; and filter out secret/API-key patterns.

findings.title: STT/TTS Configuration & Language Code Mismatches: EARS_PRIMARY_PROVIDER Ignored, 3-Letter ISO Codes Dropped by Groq Whisper, and Invalid OPENAI_API_KEY Breaks RealtimeMouth Local Fallback
findings.component: Backend Voice Routes & RealtimeMouth Fallback (voice.ts / RealtimeMouth.cs)
findings.description:
Multiple configuration and protocol mismatches exist between the C# voice/dictation clients and src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:
1. Ignored .env provider settings: src/backend/.env defines EARS_PRIMARY_PROVIDER=groq and DICTATION_CLEANUP_PROVIDER=groq, but src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts never reads process.env.EARS_PRIMARY_PROVIDER or process.env.DICTATION_CLEANUP_PROVIDER; the provider order is hardcoded as Groq -> Gemini -> Deepgram (for STT) and Groq -> Gemini -> OpenAI (for cleanup).
2. 3-letter ISO language codes dropped in Groq Whisper STT: DictationLanguageCatalog.Specific (DictationLanguageCatalog.cs:11-94) includes five 3-letter language codes ('yue' Cantonese, 'fil' Filipino, 'ceb' Cebuano, 'rup' Aromanian, 'kea' Cape Verdean). However, voice.ts:705 checks if (normalizedLang.length === 2) before appending language to the Groq Whisper form data, silently dropping all 3-letter codes and forcing auto-detect.
3. /v2/dictation/gemini-token ignores body.keyterms and body.language: DictationController passes the user's custom vocabulary (keyterms) and language to POST /v2/dictation/gemini-token, but voice.ts:58-75 never reads body.keyterms or body.language when building the setup object.
4. RealtimeMouth fallback broken when OPENAI_API_KEY is present but Realtime session minting fails: In voice.ts:146-197 (handleRealtimeSession), the default model is 'gpt-realtime-2.1-mini' (line 161). When OPENAI_API_KEY is set in .env, calling https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/sessions with 'gpt-realtime-2.1-mini' (or an invalid/expired key) fails, and the catch block at line 197 returns client_secret: { value: openAiKey } (which starts with 'sk-...'). However, RealtimeMouth.ConnectAsync (RealtimeMouth.cs:355) ONLY activates useLocalHttpTts fallback if secret.StartsWith('ek_kursor_')! When it receives 'sk-...', RealtimeMouth attempts a direct browser-style WebSocket connection to wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1-mini with OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1, which fails and breaks TTS instead of falling back to /agent/realtime/speak.
reproductionSteps: Inspect voice.ts:146-197 and RealtimeMouth.cs:345-378: when OPENAI_API_KEY is set to 'sk-...' and /v1/realtime/sessions returns HTTP 400/401, handleRealtimeSession returns value: 'sk-...'.
Observe that RealtimeMouth.cs:355 checks secret.StartsWith('ek_kursor_') and therefore does NOT enable useLocalHttpTts fallback.
Inspect voice.ts:705 and verify 3-letter language codes ('yue', 'fil') fail normalizedLang.length === 2.

findings.title: README.md and docs/04 claim nonexistent `writeOnPage` / `callout` / `brace` / `table` / `chart` primitives and misdescribe `openPage` as a study-card builder
findings.description: README.md (lines 20-21) states that Kursor's Interactive Sticky Notes & Screen Ink Notebook uses `openPage` + `writeOnPage` to spawn draggable, expandable on-screen study cards with markdown headings, bullet lists, and math steps. In reality, `writeOnPage` does not exist anywhere in `clicky-draw-pieces.js`, `clicky-draw-engine.js`, or `clicky-draw-native.js` (calling it throws `ReferenceError: writeOnPage is not defined`), and `openPage(url)` (clicky-draw-pieces.js:460) emits an invisible action dot (`{role: 'open', payload: String(url)}`) that opens an HTTP/HTTPS URL in the user's browser on the final beat. Furthermore, `docs/04-drawing-2d-3d-and-ink-engine.md` (lines 31, 35) lists `callout`, `brace`, `table`, and `chart` as engine primitives, none of which exist in `makeApi` or `clicky-draw-pieces.js`.
reproductionSteps: Run `node tests/audit/ws-fg/test-2d-engine.mjs`.

Inspect program `21_openPage_url_action_AUD_F_001` (`openPage("https://example.com/docs")`) and program `22_writeOnPage_hallucinated_primitive_AUD_F_001` (`writeOnPage("Study Card", "Markdown body")`) in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-fg/test-2d-engine-output.json`, as well as `missingPrimitives`.
findings.observedResult: README.md (lines 20-21) states that Kursor's Interactive Sticky Notes & Screen Ink Notebook uses `openPage` + `writeOnPage` to spawn draggable, expandable on-screen study cards with markdown headings, bullet lists, and math steps. In reality, `writeOnPage` does not exist anywhere in `clicky-draw-pieces.js`, `clicky-draw-engine.js`, or `clicky-draw-native.js` (calling it throws `ReferenceError: writeOnPage is not defined`), and `openPage(url)` (clicky-draw-pieces.js:460) emits an invisible action dot (`{role: 'open', payload: String(url)}`) that opens an HTTP/HTTPS URL in the user's browser on the final beat. Furthermore, `docs/04-drawing-2d-3d-and-ink-engine.md` (lines 31, 35) lists `callout`, `brace`, `table`, and `chart` as engine primitives, none of which exist in `makeApi` or `clicky-draw-pieces.js`.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Any developer, prompt, or test relying on `README.md` or `docs/04` to create study cards via `openPage` + `writeOnPage` or draw tables/charts via `table()`/`chart()`/`callout()`/`brace()` will trigger runtime `ReferenceError` failures in V8.
findings.remediation: Update `README.md:20-21` and `docs/04-drawing-2d-3d-and-ink-engine.md:31,35` to document the actual card primitives (`paper`, `sticky`, `receipt`, `clipping`, `legend`) and graph/timeline APIs (`graph`, `timeline`), and remove nonexistent primitive names.

findings.title: `spot()` primitive is missing from `clicky-draw-pieces.js` despite being documented in `docs/04` and polyfilled in `brain.ts` fallback
findings.description: `clicky-draw-pieces.js:180` defines `point(x, y, name)` to ring and label a screen coordinate, but does not define `spot(x, y, name)`. `docs/04-drawing-2d-3d-and-ink-engine.md` (lines 29, 31, 181) documents `spot()` as the primary pointer primitive, and `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:911-914` (`buildLocalFallbackProgram`) has to inject an inline workaround `const spot = typeof point === "function" ? point : () => {};` before calling `spot(500, 300, "Kursor Active")`. Any LLM response that emits `spot(...)` without that inline polyfill fails at runtime with `ReferenceError: spot is not defined`.
reproductionSteps: Run `node tests/audit/ws-fg/test-2d-engine.mjs`.
Compare program `03_spot_undefined_without_polyfill_AUD_F_002` against `04_spot_with_brain_ts_polyfill` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-fg/test-2d-engine-output.json`.
findings.observedResult: `clicky-draw-pieces.js:180` defines `point(x, y, name)` to ring and label a screen coordinate, but does not define `spot(x, y, name)`. `docs/04-drawing-2d-3d-and-ink-engine.md` (lines 29, 31, 181) documents `spot()` as the primary pointer primitive, and `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:911-914` (`buildLocalFallbackProgram`) has to inject an inline workaround `const spot = typeof point === "function" ? point : () => {};` before calling `spot(500, 300, "Kursor Active")`. Any LLM response that emits `spot(...)` without that inline polyfill fails at runtime with `ReferenceError: spot is not defined`.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: LLM-generated ClickyDraw programs that call `spot(x, y, label)` (a frequent model hallucination/synonym for `point`) crash at the `spot()` statement and drop all subsequent drawing marks in that beat.
findings.remediation: Add `const spot = point` in `src/desktop/Kursor.Drawing/Assets/Engine/clicky-draw-pieces.js` right after `const point = ...` (line 184).

findings.title: `ONE_BRAIN_DRAWING_AND_3D_INSTRUCTIONS` in `brain.ts` teaches unsupported 3D material names `"cast"` and `"carbon"`
findings.description: `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:88` instructs the LLM that valid 3D materials are `"steel"|"alu"|"brass"|"copper"|"chrome"|"cast"|"titanium"|"gold"|"carbon"|"rubber"|"glass"|"wood"|"ceramic"|"plastic"|"paint:red"|"glow:cyan"`. However, neither `"cast"` nor `"carbon"` exists in `FIGURE_MATERIALS` (`clicky-draw-engine.js:561-562`, which instead has `'iron'` and `'black'`) or in `Material3D.Studio` (`Material3D.cs:85-211`). When `mat: "cast"` or `mat: "carbon"` is used, `FIGURE_MATERIALS.includes(kind)` is `false`, so `clicky-draw-engine.js:638-640` rewrites `material` to `{ mat: 'gloss', tint: 'cast' }` (or `'carbon'`). Subsequently, `Material3D.Studio` fails to parse `'cast'`/`'carbon'` as a hex color in `Math3D.LinearColor` and renders light-grey glossy plastic (`#B9BEC4`, roughness 0.22, metallic 0) instead of dark cast iron or matte carbon fiber.
reproductionSteps: Run `node tests/audit/ws-fg/test-2d-engine.mjs`.
Inspect program `34_figure_materials_and_around_audit_AUD_F_003_004` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-fg/test-2d-engine-output.json`.
findings.observedResult: `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:88` instructs the LLM that valid 3D materials are `"steel"|"alu"|"brass"|"copper"|"chrome"|"cast"|"titanium"|"gold"|"carbon"|"rubber"|"glass"|"wood"|"ceramic"|"plastic"|"paint:red"|"glow:cyan"`. However, neither `"cast"` nor `"carbon"` exists in `FIGURE_MATERIALS` (`clicky-draw-engine.js:561-562`, which instead has `'iron'` and `'black'`) or in `Material3D.Studio` (`Material3D.cs:85-211`). When `mat: "cast"` or `mat: "carbon"` is used, `FIGURE_MATERIALS.includes(kind)` is `false`, so `clicky-draw-engine.js:638-640` rewrites `material` to `{ mat: 'gloss', tint: 'cast' }` (or `'carbon'`). Subsequently, `Material3D.Studio` fails to parse `'cast'`/`'carbon'` as a hex color in `Math3D.LinearColor` and renders light-grey glossy plastic (`#B9BEC4`, roughness 0.22, metallic 0) instead of dark cast iron or matte carbon fiber.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: 3D parts assigned `mat: "cast"` or `mat: "carbon"` by OneBrain lose their dark metallic/matte appearance and render as pale grey glossy plastic.
findings.remediation: Replace `"cast"` and `"carbon"` with `"iron"` and `"black"` in `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:88`, or add `"cast"` and `"carbon"` aliases to `FIGURE_MATERIALS` (`clicky-draw-engine.js:561`) and `Material3D.Studio` (`Material3D.cs:85`).

findings.title: `OverlayWindow` ignores `WM_DPICHANGED` (`0x02E0`) and `MoveTo()` does not refresh `scale` across mixed-DPI monitors
findings.description: `OverlayWindow.Fit(int widthPx, int heightPx)` (`OverlayWindow.cs:220-226`) queries `GetDpiForWindow(Handle)` and updates `scale = dpi / 96f`, `Root.Scale`, and `Root.Size`. However, `Fit()` is only called from `ShowOver()` and `Reframe()`. `WindowProcedure` (`OverlayWindow.cs:338-407`) does not handle `WM_DPICHANGED` (`0x02E0`), and `MoveTo(int x, int y)` (`OverlayWindow.cs:462-466`, called during interactive card dragging in `CardHandles.ContinueDrag` and `PinnedCards`) moves the HWND via `SetWindowPos` without updating `scale` or `Root.Scale` when crossing onto a monitor with a different DPI.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `OverlayWindow.cs:220-226` (`Fit`), `OverlayWindow.cs:338-407` (`WindowProcedure`), and `OverlayWindow.cs:462-466` (`MoveTo`).
findings.observedResult: `OverlayWindow.Fit(int widthPx, int heightPx)` (`OverlayWindow.cs:220-226`) queries `GetDpiForWindow(Handle)` and updates `scale = dpi / 96f`, `Root.Scale`, and `Root.Size`. However, `Fit()` is only called from `ShowOver()` and `Reframe()`. `WindowProcedure` (`OverlayWindow.cs:338-407`) does not handle `WM_DPICHANGED` (`0x02E0`), and `MoveTo(int x, int y)` (`OverlayWindow.cs:462-466`, called during interactive card dragging in `CardHandles.ContinueDrag` and `PinnedCards`) moves the HWND via `SetWindowPos` without updating `scale` or `Root.Scale` when crossing onto a monitor with a different DPI.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Dragging pinned study cards or moving interactive overlays between a 100% DPI external monitor and a 150%/200% DPI laptop screen results in mis-scaled visuals and offset pointer hitboxes.
findings.remediation: Handle `WM_DPICHANGED` (`0x02E0`) in `OverlayWindow.WindowProcedure` and check `GetDpiForWindow(Handle)` in `OverlayWindow.MoveTo` to update `scale`, `Root.Scale`, and window pixel bounds when DPI changes.

findings.title: `Mp4VideoWriter` lacks input dimension validation (odd/zero dimensions) and overflows `int` bitrate arithmetic before `long` cast
findings.description: `Mp4VideoWriter` (`Mp4VideoWriter.cs:5`) is a `public sealed class` whose constructor (`Mp4VideoWriter.cs:41-60`) passes `width` and `height` directly to Media Foundation's H.264 encoder without validating that `width > 0`, `height > 0`, and both are even integers (H.264 requires even width/height). Furthermore, line 50 computes `Math.Min(2147483647L, width * height * 6)` where `width * height * 6` is evaluated in 32-bit signed `int` arithmetic before widening to `long` (`2147483647L`). Additionally, in `LessonVideoRecorder.Cancel()` (`LessonVideoRecorder.cs:158-167`), `Task.Run` joins the recording thread and deletes the output file asynchronously in the background without `Dispose()` waiting on that task.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `Mp4VideoWriter.cs:41-60` and `LessonVideoRecorder.cs:158-174`.
findings.observedResult: `Mp4VideoWriter` (`Mp4VideoWriter.cs:5`) is a `public sealed class` whose constructor (`Mp4VideoWriter.cs:41-60`) passes `width` and `height` directly to Media Foundation's H.264 encoder without validating that `width > 0`, `height > 0`, and both are even integers (H.264 requires even width/height). Furthermore, line 50 computes `Math.Min(2147483647L, width * height * 6)` where `width * height * 6` is evaluated in 32-bit signed `int` arithmetic before widening to `long` (`2147483647L`). Additionally, in `LessonVideoRecorder.Cancel()` (`LessonVideoRecorder.cs:158-167`), `Task.Run` joins the recording thread and deletes the output file asynchronously in the background without `Dispose()` waiting on that task.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Direct callers of `Mp4VideoWriter` with non-even monitor crop sizes fail with raw `COMException`, and `LessonVideoRecorder.Cancel()` can race with immediate file cleanup.
findings.remediation: Validate and round `width` and `height` to even positive bounds in `Mp4VideoWriter`, change bitrate calculation to `(uint)Math.Min(2147483647L, (long)width * height * 6L)`, and track the cancellation `Task` in `LessonVideoRecorder`.

findings.title: `ONE_BRAIN_DRAWING_AND_3D_INSTRUCTIONS` in `brain.ts` teaches `top` radius on `f.cone(...)`, which `clicky-three-parts.js` completely ignores
findings.description: In `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:74`, `ONE_BRAIN_DRAWING_AND_3D_INSTRUCTIONS` teaches the LLM to build truncated cones/nozzles using `f.cone({ at: [x,y,z], r: 0.6, top: 0.2, h: 0.7, axis: "x"|"y"|"z", mat: "alu", name: "Nozzle" })`. However, `SHAPES.cone(o)` in `clicky-three-parts.js:372-377` never reads `o.top`—it always constructs a pointed cone with apex `[0, h / 2]` (`new T.ConeGeometry(r, h, ...)`). Only `SHAPES.cyl(o)` (`clicky-three-parts.js:365-371`) reads `o.top` to construct a frustum.
reproductionSteps: Run `node tests/audit/ws-fg/test-3d-engine.mjs`.
Inspect `coneTopParameterIgnoredByteIdentical` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-fg/test-3d-engine-output.json`.
findings.observedResult: In `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:74`, `ONE_BRAIN_DRAWING_AND_3D_INSTRUCTIONS` teaches the LLM to build truncated cones/nozzles using `f.cone({ at: [x,y,z], r: 0.6, top: 0.2, h: 0.7, axis: "x"|"y"|"z", mat: "alu", name: "Nozzle" })`. However, `SHAPES.cone(o)` in `clicky-three-parts.js:372-377` never reads `o.top`—it always constructs a pointed cone with apex `[0, h / 2]` (`new T.ConeGeometry(r, h, ...)`). Only `SHAPES.cyl(o)` (`clicky-three-parts.js:365-371`) reads `o.top` to construct a frustum.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Whenever OneBrain follows its own prompt example (`f.cone({ r: 0.6, top: 0.2, h: 0.7, name: "Nozzle" })`), nozzles and frustums render as sharp pointed cones instead of truncated cones.
findings.remediation: In `clicky-three-parts.js:372`, if `num(o.top, 0) > 0`, forward `SHAPES.cone(o)` to `SHAPES.cyl(o)`, and remove misleading `top: 0.2` from `f.cone` in `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:74`.

findings.title: `ThreeStage.Dispose()` disposes D3D11/D2D1 GPU resources on `ThreadPool` even if `frameThread.Join(5000)` times out, racing with active rendering
findings.description: In `ThreeStage.Dispose()` (`ThreeStage.cs:1083-1107`), if `frameThread.IsAlive` is true, `Dispose()` queues a background work item via `ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem`: `running.Join(5000); Release();`. If `running.Join(5000)` times out after 5 seconds (for example, if `frameThread` is blocked in `WaitForCompositorFrame` or V8 `RunTicks`), `Release()` (`ThreeStage.cs:1110-1120`) still executes unconditionally on the ThreadPool thread, calling `d2dTarget.Dispose()`, `backBuffer.Dispose()`, `renderer.Dispose()`, and `wake.Dispose()` while `frameThread` is still running and accessing those exact native COM pointers (`d2d`, `renderer`, `backBuffer`, `wake`).
reproductionSteps: Inspect `ThreeStage.cs:1083-1120` (`Dispose` and `Release`) and `ThreeStage.cs:1330-1375` (`FrameLoop`).

findings.title: ClickyThreeKernel Thread-Safety Race on V8ScriptEngine Disposal, Missing V8 Heap/Execution Constraints, and Unconditional Disposal of Active Stage GPU Buffers on Idle Timeout
findings.description: ClickyThreeKernel has three compounding lifecycle defects: (1) Lock asymmetry on engine and loadFailed: WarmUp() (lines 98-105) reads engine and loadFailed under lock (gate), and HeapBytes (line 73) calls engine?.GetRuntimeHeapInfo().TotalHeapSize without any lock, while Run() (lines 181-186) disposes engine and sets engine = null and LoadIfNeeded() (lines 290-311) assigns engine and loadFailed on the worker thread without acquiring lock (gate). Calling HeapBytes while Run() disposes engine can throw ObjectDisposedException or access a torn reference. (2) Unbounded V8 execution: LoadIfNeeded() (line 290) creates V8ScriptEngine without V8RuntimeConstraints or an Interrupt() timeout around buildFunction.Invoke(false, kind, recipe) (line 349). (3) Premature GPU buffer disposal while stages are still live: When work.TryTake times out after IdleRelease (5 minutes without new shape builds), ReleaseCachedGpuBuffers() (lines 244-274) unconditionally disposes item.Gpu (ID3D11Buffer vertex/index buffers) and sets item.Gpu = null on every cached Mesh3D before checking if (ThreeStage.LiveCounts.Stages == 0) at line 269, racing with any open ThreeStage render thread reading mesh.Gpu.

findings.title: OverlayHost Never Unregisters from ScreenCaptureYield and FramePacer Leaks Kernel Waitable Timer
findings.description: OverlayHost.CreateOverlayWindow registers its HWND with both CaptureExclusion.Register and ScreenCaptureYield.Register (line 528), but ThreadMain's finally block (lines 367-371) only calls CaptureExclusion.Unregister(WindowHandle) and never calls ScreenCaptureYield.Unregister(WindowHandle), leaving a destroyed HWND in ScreenCaptureYield.overlayHwnds. findings.title: GraphicsCaptureSource Frame Leak on Timeout Race, Multi-GPU Adapter Mismatch, and Stale Static WinRT Device
findings.description: 1) In GraphicsCaptureSource.CaptureMonitor, framePool.FrameArrived calls firstFrame.TrySetResult(pool.TryGetNextFrame()); if the 250ms timeout or an earlier frame wins the race, the newly acquired Direct3D11CaptureFrame is rejected by TrySetResult and leaked without Dispose(). 2) ScreenCaptureService.TryCaptureWithGraphicsCaptureAsync hardcodes gpu = gpus[0] (line 396) instead of selecting the CaptureGpu that owns the target display. 3) GraphicsCaptureSource caches a static winrtDevice tied to winrtDeviceOwner without invalidating it cleanly if that CaptureGpu is disposed while another GPU is used. 4) DesktopDuplicationSource.TryCapture ignores frameInfo.ProtectedContentMaskedOut, returning blacked-out frames without signalling protected content.

findings.title: DictationTextTarget.BlindPasteAsync and TextInsertion.SnapshotClipboard Permanently Destroy User Clipboard Data
findings.description: 1) DictationTextTarget.BlindPasteAsync invokes TextInsertion.PasteTextAsync(text, restoreClipboard: false) for apps in BlindPasteProcesses (WeChat, ms-teams, ChatGPT, Codex, sublime_text, ApplicationFrameHost) and fallback paths, permanently overwriting the user's clipboard with dictated text. 2) Even when restoreClipboard: true is used, TextInsertion.SnapshotClipboard() skips handle-based formats (CF_BITMAP, CF_DSPBITMAP, CF_METAFILEPICT, CF_ENHMETAFILE, CF_PALETTE) and payloads exceeding 64 MB, and then calls EmptyClipboard(), permanently destroying copied images or large clipboard items.

findings.title: RecentFiles.Target Binary .lnk Parser Lacks Bounds Checks and Enables Silent Arbitrary File Exfiltration via Window Titles
findings.description: RecentFiles.Target(shortcutPath) manually parses raw .lnk binary bytes without sufficient bounds validation: line 78 reads BitConverter.ToUInt16(array, num2) when array.Length == 76 and (num & 1) != 0 (throwing ArgumentOutOfRangeException); lines 94-95 read 32-bit offsets at num3 + 28 and num3 + 32 after only checking num2 + 28 <= array.Length at line 80; and ReadUnicode(array, num3 + num5) (line 130) does not validate that at >= 0 or at < data.Length. findings.title: LowLevelInputHub.CheckHookAlive Raw-Input Replay Bypasses ClickyUserInputBlocker.ShouldHoldKey

findings.title: Unsynchronized Dictionary Mutations and Race Conditions in ClickyInkNoteStore and ClickyLiveNoteStore
findings.description: ClickyInkNoteStore and ClickyLiveNoteStore store state in standard non-concurrent Dictionary<,> and HashSet<> fields (versionsByNoteId, selectedVersionByNoteId, lastDocumentByNoteId, liveNotes, settledNotes, watched, pendingStreamedTexts) without any lock or synchronization. findings.description: DocumentText.ReadSystemDocument (line 188) checks only the compressed archive file size on disk (new FileInfo(path).Length > 67108864, 64 MB), and ReadEntry(ZipArchiveEntry) (lines 242-247) calls streamReader.ReadToEnd() without checking entry.Length or capping the number of characters read from the deflate stream, followed by full-document regex matches (WordXmlToText, SharedStringItem, DrawingTextRun) before Cap(text, 60000) is ever invoked. findings.title: Unadapted macOS Tool Name (mac_step) and Platform References Across TurnPromptBuilder, ClickyBrowserBridge, and clicky-harness.exe
findings.component: Agent Prompt Builder, Browser Bridge & Harness Instructions
findings.description: Although WindowsInstructionAdapter.Adapt() (WindowsInstructionAdapter.cs:11-56) scrubs 'macOS'/'Mac'/'mdfind' from BundledResources/clicky-model-instructions.md, several runtime prompt builders bypass WindowsInstructionAdapter and inject macOS-specific tool names and strings directly into Windows agent turns: (1) TurnPromptBuilder.BuildFirstTurnPrompt() (TurnPromptBuilder.cs:38) injects 'To use any other desktop app on the user's computer, call the mac_step tool (HeyClicky's screen agent)'; (2) ClickyBrowserBridge.cs:261, 879, 962 returns tool guidance referencing 'mac_step' when Chrome is unavailable or on a restricted page; (3) AgentHarnessNames.WireValue(AgentHarnessPlace.Mac) (AgentHarnessNames.cs:55) uses the wire token 'mac' on Windows; (4) clicky-harness.exe (agents-harness-drivers.txt:65-66) injects '<their_skills> The user's own skills, kept on this Mac' even when $f (Windows) is true, and its fetch_url tool sends a hardcoded 'Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7' User-Agent header.

findings.title: RoutineScheduler Holds Indefinite Win32 System Sleep Lock (PowerRequestSystemRequired) Whenever Any Routine Is Unpaused on AC Power
findings.description: In RoutineScheduler.cs:112 and 307-309, RefreshKeepAwake() calls RoutineKeepAwake.Update(routines.Any((ClickyRoutine r) => !r.IsPaused)). Inside RoutineKeepAwake.Reconcile() (lines 46-68), whenever _hasUnpausedRoutines && OnAcPower() is true, it creates a Win32 power request ('HeyClicky scheduled routines') and calls PowerSetRequest(_request, PowerRequestType.PowerRequestSystemRequired) (value 1) and holds it indefinitely. Consequently, if a user has even a single weekly or daily routine enabled while plugged into AC power, Kursor prevents the Windows PC from ever entering system sleep—even when no routine is running and the next scheduled run is days away.
reproductionSteps: Run Scenario 29 in tests/audit/ws-jk/test-agents-harness.ps1.
Inspect RoutineScheduler.cs:112, 307-309 and RoutineKeepAwake.cs:46-68.
With one unpaused routine and AC power connected, run 'powercfg /requests' in an elevated prompt to observe the persistent SYSTEM power request.
findings.observedResult: In RoutineScheduler.cs:112 and 307-309, RefreshKeepAwake() calls RoutineKeepAwake.Update(routines.Any((ClickyRoutine r) => !r.IsPaused)). Inside RoutineKeepAwake.Reconcile() (lines 46-68), whenever _hasUnpausedRoutines && OnAcPower() is true, it creates a Win32 power request ('HeyClicky scheduled routines') and calls PowerSetRequest(_request, PowerRequestType.PowerRequestSystemRequired) (value 1) and holds it indefinitely. Consequently, if a user has even a single weekly or daily routine enabled while plugged into AC power, Kursor prevents the Windows PC from ever entering system sleep—even when no routine is running and the next scheduled run is days away.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Prevents desktop and laptop PCs on AC power from ever sleeping once a user creates any scheduled routine, wasting energy and violating Windows power management expectations.
findings.remediation: Acquire PowerRequestSystemRequired only while a routine is actively running in FireAsync() (or make 'Prevent sleep on AC power for routines' an explicit opt-in toggle in Settings).

findings.category: Hardcoded Production URL & Plaintext Credential Storage
findings.title: CodexHomeManager.cs hardcodes https://worker.heyclicky.com/agent/openai/v1 and writes plaintext session tokens, bearer tokens, and sandbox_mode = 'danger-full-access' to %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\codex-home\ even though local Codex is retired

Root cause: CodexHomeManager.cs:15 hardcodes OpenAiBaseUrl = 'https://worker.heyclicky.com/agent/openai/v1' and serializes credentials into config.toml and auth.json even though AgentHarnessRuntimes.cs:16-19 retired local Codex.

findings.title: POST /proactive/jobs resets nextSuggestionNumericId = 101 in memory on every backend restart, colliding with existing SQLite proactive_cards rows and un-dismissing previously dismissed proactive suggestions
findings.description: After a backend restart, POST /proactive/jobs reuses IDs '101', '102', ... and executes ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ... dismissed = 0, overwriting and un-dismissing resolved proactive cards in SQLite. Root cause: let nextSuggestionNumericId = 101 (agents.ts:85) is not seeded from SQLite proactive_cards at startup.
reproductionSteps: Create and dismiss suggestion 101, restart the backend, and call POST /proactive/jobs -> row '101' is overwritten with dismissed = 0.
findings.observedResult: After a backend restart, POST /proactive/jobs reuses IDs '101', '102', ... and executes ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET ... dismissed = 0, overwriting and un-dismissing resolved proactive cards in SQLite.
findings.expectedResult: New proactive suggestions after a backend restart receive strictly increasing IDs and never overwrite existing proactive_cards rows.
findings.impact: Dismissed proactive agent cards reappear after backend restarts.
findings.remediation: Seed nextSuggestionNumericId from SELECT COALESCE(MAX(CAST(id AS INTEGER)), 100) + 1 FROM proactive_cards at startup.

findings.title: DeveloperFlags.FullAgentActivity Getter Hardcoded to false and Developer Settings Page Hidden Behind Server Flag

findings.title: Dead/Duplicate JsonAppSettings Class Uses Incompatible settings.json Schema and --background Startup Flag
findings.description: Kursor.App contains two competing IAppSettings implementations: CoreAppSettings (which wraps HeyClicky.Core.Settings.SettingsStore and persists the full AppSettings schema to %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\settings.json) and JsonAppSettings (a 651-line standalone class with its own source-generated serializer for a 10-field Data class that also defaults to Path.Combine(AppPaths.Root, "settings.json")). If JsonAppSettings is instantiated with its default directory and Save() is called (line 643), it overwrites %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\settings.json with only 10 PascalCase properties, wiping out hotkeys, audio devices, dictation words, and agent preferences. Furthermore, JsonAppSettings.LaunchAtLogin (line 611) writes '"<exe>" --background' to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, whereas Program.cs / LaunchAtLogin.cs expects '--autostart'.

If JsonAppSettings is instantiated with its default directory and Save() is called (line 643), it overwrites %LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\settings.json with only 10 PascalCase properties, wiping out hotkeys, audio devices, dictation words, and agent preferences. findings.title: Unguarded async void UI Entrypoints and Fire-and-Forget Spreadsheet Loader Risk Unhandled Exceptions and Infinite Spinner
findings.component: Notch Drawing Viewer / AppHost Cursor Dock / Spreadsheet Document View

findings.title: `seed-local-auth.ps1` Writes PascalCase `endpoints.json` Ignored by Case-Sensitive `AppBundleConfiguration.ReadConfigured` and Leaves Redundant Plaintext `session.json` on Disk
findings.description: In `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:70-75`, the script writes `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\endpoints.json` with PascalCase keys (`WorkerBaseUrl`, `SupabaseUrl`, `SupabaseAnonKey`). However, in `src/desktop/Kursor.Core/HeyClicky.Core.Configuration/AppBundleConfiguration.cs:78-80, 147-159`, `ReadConfigured(string configPath)` parses the JSON using `JsonDocument.Parse` and calls case-sensitive `rootElement.TryGetProperty("workerBaseUrl", ...)`, `TryGetProperty("supabaseUrl", ...)`, and `TryGetProperty("supabaseAnonKey", ...)` (`camelCase`). As a result, all 3 properties in `endpoints.json` evaluate to `null` and `endpoints.json` is completely ignored (only falling back to `AssemblyMetadataAttribute` defaults compiled into `HeyClicky.dll`). Furthermore, `seed-local-auth.ps1:54-68` writes plaintext tokens (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\session.json`, which `AuthTokenStore.cs` never reads (it only reads DPAPI-encrypted `auth.localdev.bin` and `auth.bin`).
reproductionSteps: Inspect `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:54-75` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\endpoints.json`.

Compare the PascalCase keys (`WorkerBaseUrl`, `SupabaseUrl`, `SupabaseAnonKey`) with `AppBundleConfiguration.ReadConfigured` (`AppBundleConfiguration.cs:78-80, 147-159`), which queries `workerBaseUrl`, `supabaseUrl`, and `supabaseAnonKey` via case-sensitive `JsonElement.TryGetProperty`.
Inspect `AuthTokenStore.cs:20-85` to verify that `session.json` is never read by the desktop client.

As a result, all 3 properties in `endpoints.json` evaluate to `null` and `endpoints.json` is completely ignored (only falling back to `AssemblyMetadataAttribute` defaults compiled into `HeyClicky.dll`). Furthermore, `seed-local-auth.ps1:54-68` writes plaintext tokens (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\session.json`, which `AuthTokenStore.cs` never reads (it only reads DPAPI-encrypted `auth.localdev.bin` and `auth.bin`).

findings.title: Unstripped Base64 Screenshots Persisted in SQLite `threads.messages_json`, Plaintext Dictation & BrowserBridge Token Files on Disk, and Residual Vendor Telemetry Keys
findings.description: A full data-at-rest and data-in-transit inventory revealed four privacy/data-handling gaps: 1) While the desktop client (`BrainSession.cs:931`) explicitly calls `WithoutScreenshots(thread)` to strip base64 JPEGs before writing `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\OneBrain\<userId>\threads\<id>.json`, the backend's `ensureSessionAndThread` (`src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:171-186`, called at lines `980` and `1128`) serializes the entire `incomingThread` array—including any `input_image` `data:image/jpeg;base64,...` blocks in the thread history—directly into SQLite `threads.messages_json` without stripping image payloads. 2) `DictationTranscriptArchive.AppendAsync` (`DictationTranscriptArchive.cs:23-49`) appends every dictated sentence and active application name in plaintext JSONL to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` for 14 days (4 files / 8 utterances found on disk). 3) `ClickyBrowserBridge.WriteConnectionFile` (`ClickyBrowserBridge.cs:256-267`) writes the loopback MCP bearer token in plaintext to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\BrowserBridge\connection.json` (verified live on port 51635: any local process reading `connection.json` can invoke `tools/list` and control the user's Chrome tabs). 4) `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:15-17` still compiles in the vendor's production `HeyClicky.PostHogApiKey`, `HeyClicky.SentryDsn`, and `HeyClicky.UpdateFeedUrl`, and `CrashReporting.cs:242` sets `SendDefaultPii = true` whenever the Sentry DSN is active.
reproductionSteps: Send a `/brain/turn` request containing an `input_image` block (`data:image/jpeg;base64,...`) in `thread` and query `SELECT length(messages_json), messages_json FROM threads WHERE id = ?` in `src/backend/data/kursor.db` (`poc4_sqliteBase64ScreenshotPersistence` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/security-pocs.json`).
Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/privacy-data-inventory.json` and `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/ipc-and-protocol-checks.json`.
findings.observedResult: A full data-at-rest and data-in-transit inventory revealed four privacy/data-handling gaps: 1) While the desktop client (`BrainSession.cs:931`) explicitly calls `WithoutScreenshots(thread)` to strip base64 JPEGs before writing `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\OneBrain\<userId>\threads\<id>.json`, the backend's `ensureSessionAndThread` (`src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:171-186`, called at lines `980` and `1128`) serializes the entire `incomingThread` array—including any `input_image` `data:image/jpeg;base64,...` blocks in the thread history—directly into SQLite `threads.messages_json` without stripping image payloads. 2) `DictationTranscriptArchive.AppendAsync` (`DictationTranscriptArchive.cs:23-49`) appends every dictated sentence and active application name in plaintext JSONL to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\DictationTranscripts\YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` for 14 days (4 files / 8 utterances found on disk). 3) `ClickyBrowserBridge.WriteConnectionFile` (`ClickyBrowserBridge.cs:256-267`) writes the loopback MCP bearer token in plaintext to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\BrowserBridge\connection.json` (verified live on port 51635: any local process reading `connection.json` can invoke `tools/list` and control the user's Chrome tabs). 4) `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:15-17` still compiles in the vendor's production `HeyClicky.PostHogApiKey`, `HeyClicky.SentryDsn`, and `HeyClicky.UpdateFeedUrl`, and `CrashReporting.cs:242` sets `SendDefaultPii = true` whenever the Sentry DSN is active.

findings.title: Unsigned Rebuilt Managed Assemblies (`HeyClicky*.dll`) Loaded by Signed `HeyClicky.exe` Apphost and Unfiltered `SingleInstance` IPC Argument Forwarding
findings.description: In `dist/kursor-desktop/`, the native .NET apphost `HeyClicky.exe` retains the original vendor's `Valid` Authenticode signature, whereas all 7 rebuilt managed assemblies (`HeyClicky.dll`, `HeyClicky.Core.dll`, `HeyClicky.Platform.dll`, `HeyClicky.Agents.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing3D.dll`, `HeyClicky.Contracts.dll`) are `NotSigned`. Additionally, in `SingleInstance.cs:213-229`, `MemoryMappedFile.CreateOrOpen` and `NamedPipeServerStream` are created with default security descriptors (`writableByAnySameUserProcess: true` verified in `ipc-and-protocol-checks.json`), and `ReadActivationPayloadAsync` (`lines 368-408`) accepts up to 1 MB of arbitrary strings over the named pipe and passes them directly to `OnSecondaryArguments` (`Program.cs:179-196`) without filtering non-URI arguments.
reproductionSteps: Run `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky.exe` and `dist\kursor-desktop\HeyClicky*.dll` (`authenticode` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/env-and-surface-inventory.json`).
Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/ipc-and-protocol-checks.json` (`writableByAnySameUserProcess: true`) and `SingleInstance.cs:213-229, 368-408`.
findings.observedResult: In `dist/kursor-desktop/`, the native .NET apphost `HeyClicky.exe` retains the original vendor's `Valid` Authenticode signature, whereas all 7 rebuilt managed assemblies (`HeyClicky.dll`, `HeyClicky.Core.dll`, `HeyClicky.Platform.dll`, `HeyClicky.Agents.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing.dll`, `HeyClicky.Drawing3D.dll`, `HeyClicky.Contracts.dll`) are `NotSigned`. Additionally, in `SingleInstance.cs:213-229`, `MemoryMappedFile.CreateOrOpen` and `NamedPipeServerStream` are created with default security descriptors (`writableByAnySameUserProcess: true` verified in `ipc-and-protocol-checks.json`), and `ReadActivationPayloadAsync` (`lines 368-408`) accepts up to 1 MB of arbitrary strings over the named pipe and passes them directly to `OnSecondaryArguments` (`Program.cs:179-196`) without filtering non-URI arguments.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Mixed vendor-signed `.exe` + unsigned `.dll` binaries can trigger Windows Defender SmartScreen/WDAC trust warnings, and any same-user process can overwrite the 4096-byte MMF pipe pointer to intercept secondary activations.
findings.remediation: Configure explicit `PipeSecurity` / `MemoryMappedFileSecurity` scoped to the current user SID in `SingleInstance.cs:213-229`, reduce `MaxPayloadBytes` from 1 MB to 8 KB, and optionally sign `dist/kursor-desktop/*.dll` with a local development certificate in `setup-kursor.ps1`.

findings.title: Unbounded SQLite `sessions`/`threads` Table & WAL Growth and Unbounded In-Memory State Maps in `agents.ts`
findings.description: 1) In `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:150-188`, `ensureSessionAndThread` inserts/updates rows in `sessions` and `threads` on every `/brain/turn` request with no row retention policy, no payload pruning, and no periodic `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`. On the live instance, `src/backend/data/kursor.db` (4.22 MB) + `kursor.db-wal` (5.84 MB) already consume 10.06 MB for just 39 sessions / 14 threads, and during our 215-turn soak test (`soak-and-recovery-log.json`), `bench-soak.db` + `-wal` grew linearly with every turn and screenshot. 2) In `src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts`, `proactiveJobs` (`line 83`), `proactiveCardStatuses` (`line 84`), `turnLeases` (`line 534`), and `calendarEvents` (`line 972`) are module-scoped in-memory `Map`s/arrays with no TTL eviction or maximum entry cap, growing monotonically over long-running backend sessions.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/privacy-data-inventory.json` (`dbFileBytes: 4222976`, `walFileBytes: 5838072`) and `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/soak-and-recovery-log.json`.
Inspect `src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:83-84, 534, 972` to verify that `proactiveJobs`, `proactiveCardStatuses`, `turnLeases`, and `calendarEvents` never evict old entries.

findings.impact: Gradual disk bloat in `src/backend/data/kursor.db*` and steady heap growth in `node.exe` during multi-day desktop sessions.
findings.remediation: Add a startup + hourly maintenance timer in `src/backend/src/db/index.ts` that prunes `threads`/`sessions` older than 30 days (or beyond 500 rows) and runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, and cap `proactiveJobs` and `turnLeases` in `src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts` to 500 entries with FIFO eviction.

findings.title: Dual Autostart Registration in `install-autostart.ps1` (`HKCU\...\Run\Kursor` + `Startup\Kursor.lnk`) Triggers Concurrent Login Startup Race
findings.description: In `scripts/install-autostart.ps1`, lines `20-26` register `HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` value `Kursor` = `wscript.exe //B //Nologo "C:\dev\heyclicky-clone\scripts\start-kursor-hidden.vbs"`, and lines `28-38` ALSO create a shortcut `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\Kursor.lnk` pointing to the exact same `wscript.exe //B //Nologo "...\start-kursor-hidden.vbs"` command! At Windows login, Explorer executes both `HKCU\...\Run` and the `Startup` folder concurrently, spawning two simultaneous instances of `start-kursor.ps1` with no cross-process lock. Both instances simultaneously run `seed-local-auth.ps1` (racing on DPAPI file writes to `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin`), both check `/health` before either backend has bound port `8787`, and both spawn `node.exe` (`npx tsx src/index.ts`) and `HeyClicky.exe` at the same time.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `scripts/install-autostart.ps1:20-38` and `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/env-and-surface-inventory.json` (`runRegistryCurrentUser.Kursor` and `startupShortcut.exists = true`).
Observe that both mechanisms invoke `wscript.exe //B //Nologo "C:\dev\heyclicky-clone\scripts\start-kursor-hidden.vbs"` at user logon without a mutex in `start-kursor.ps1`.

At Windows login, Explorer executes both `HKCU\...\Run` and the `Startup` folder concurrently, spawning two simultaneous instances of `start-kursor.ps1` with no cross-process lock. Both instances simultaneously run `seed-local-auth.ps1` (racing on DPAPI file writes to `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin`), both check `/health` before either backend has bound port `8787`, and both spawn `node.exe` (`npx tsx src/index.ts`) and `HeyClicky.exe` at the same time.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Login race condition causing duplicate `node.exe` spawns, port `8787` `EADDRINUSE` failures in `.backend.err.log`, and concurrent writes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\auth*.bin`.
findings.remediation: Remove the redundant `Startup\Kursor.lnk` creation from `scripts/install-autostart.ps1:28-38` (keep only `HKCU\...\Run\Kursor`) and acquire a system mutex at the top of `start-kursor.ps1`.

findings.title: Hardcoded Machine-Specific Paths (`C:\Users\ubaid\...` and `C:\Users\niles\...`), Missing `CodexRuntime\codex.exe`, and `dotenv.config({ override: true })` Env Override
findings.description: Three portability and reliability defects affect startup and fallback paths: 1) `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:7-8` hardcodes `const LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH = "C:\\Users\\ubaid\\AppData\\Local\\HeyClicky\\app-config.json";` instead of deriving the path from `process.env.LOCALAPPDATA`. 2) `src/desktop/Kursor.Agents/HeyClicky.Agents.Harness/AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs:75` hardcodes `"C:\\Users\\niles\\code\\clicky-closed\\windows\\src\\HeyClicky.Agents\\Harness\\AgentHarnessRunnerRuntime.cs"` as its fallback repository path, and `dist/kursor-desktop/` does not ship `CodexRuntime\codex.exe` (`codexRuntimeExists: false` in `env-and-surface-inventory.json`), causing local Codex agent sessions (`CodexSession.ResolveBundledCodexExecutablePath`) to fail when launched. 3) `src/backend/src/index.ts:2` calls `dotenv.config({ override: true })`, which overwrites `process.env.PORT`, `process.env.DATABASE_PATH`, and API key environment variables passed by parent processes whenever `src/backend/.env` exists in the working directory.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:7-8`, `src/backend/src/index.ts:1-2`, and `src/desktop/Kursor.Agents/HeyClicky.Agents.Harness/AgentHarnessRunnerProcess.cs:75`.
Check `distFiles.codexRuntimeExists` in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-lm/env-and-surface-inventory.json` (`false`).

findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Running Kursor under any Windows user account other than `ubaid` breaks `LOCAL_APP_CONFIG_PATH`, caller-supplied `PORT`/`DATABASE_PATH` env vars are ignored when `.env` is present, and local Codex CLI harness execution fails due to missing `CodexRuntime\codex.exe`.

findings.title: LoopbackHttpServer.HandleAsync Lacks Per-Connection Read Timeouts and Concurrency Limits, and ClickyBrowserBridge Leaks denied Tasks, Disconnected Profile commands, and Decompiler-Broken SplitWords Iterator
findings.description: 1) Unbounded slowloris connections on LoopbackHttpServer: In LoopbackHttpServer.cs:173, AcceptLoopAsync spawns Task.Run(() => HandleAsync(client, ct)) for every accepted socket with no maximum concurrent connection limit and no read timeout on stream.ReadAsync(chunk, ct) (lines 202, 240). Any local process opening connections to 127.0.0.1:<port> without sending '\r\n\r\n' (or sending a large Content-Length without body bytes) holds a 64 KB buffer + MemoryStream + Task open indefinitely. 2) Unbounded collection leaks in ClickyBrowserBridge: In ClickyBrowserBridge.Finish(string thread, string turn) (lines 2506, 2511-2528), every completed turn adds task to HashSet<string> denied (which is never pruned) and appends an 'operation': 'end' command object to commands[item] for every key in commands.Keys. Meanwhile, ExpirePeers() (lines 2782-2806) removes stale profiles from peers, peerBrowsers, and peerExtensions, but NEVER removes stale profiles from commands—causing commands[disconnectedProfile] to accumulate 'end' commands across every turn for the lifetime of the app. 3) Decompiler-broken iterator: ClickyBrowserBridge.SplitWords (lines 846-854) contains '//yield-return decompiler failed: Unexpected instruction in Iterator.Dispose()' and instantiates raw compiler state machine _003CSplitWords_003Ed__30.
reproductionSteps:
1. Inspect LoopbackHttpServer.cs lines 173 and 188-257.
2. Inspect ClickyBrowserBridge.cs lines 846-854, 2497-2546, and 2782-2806.
3. Observe that ExpirePeers() removes expired keys from peers/peerBrowsers/peerExtensions (lines 2792-2794) but not from commands, while Finish() appends to commands[item] for every key in commands.Keys (line 2519).
findings.observedResult: No read timeout or connection cap in LoopbackHttpServer; commands and denied grow without bound in ClickyBrowserBridge; and SplitWords uses raw _003CSplitWords_003Ed__30.
findings.expectedResult: LoopbackHttpServer.HandleAsync should enforce a 10-second CancellationTokenSource timeout per request and a SemaphoreSlim concurrency cap; ClickyBrowserBridge.ExpirePeers() should remove expired profiles from commands; denied should be bounded; and SplitWords should be a clean C# iterator.
findings.impact: 1) Unbounded slowloris connections on LoopbackHttpServer: In LoopbackHttpServer.cs:173, AcceptLoopAsync spawns Task.Run(() => HandleAsync(client, ct)) for every accepted socket with no maximum concurrent connection limit and no read timeout on stream.ReadAsync(chunk, ct) (lines 202, 240). Any local process opening connections to 127.0.0.1:<port> without sending '\r\n\r\n' (or sending a large Content-Length without body bytes) holds a 64 KB buffer + MemoryStream + Task open indefinitely. 2) Unbounded collection leaks in ClickyBrowserBridge: In ClickyBrowserBridge.Finish(string thread, string turn) (lines 2506, 2511-2528), every completed turn adds task to HashSet<string> denied (which is never pruned) and appends an 'operation': 'end' command object to commands[item] for every key in commands.Keys. Meanwhile, ExpirePeers() (lines 2782-2806) removes stale profiles from peers, peerBrowsers, and peerExtensions, but NEVER removes stale profiles from commands—causing commands[disconnectedProfile] to accumulate 'end' commands across every turn for the lifetime of the app. 3) Decompiler-broken iterator: ClickyBrowserBridge.SplitWords (lines 846-854) contains '//yield-return decompiler failed: Unexpected instruction in Iterator.Dispose()' and instantiates raw compiler state machine _003CSplitWords_003Ed__30.
findings.remediation: Add a linked CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct) with CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)) inside LoopbackHttpServer.HandleAsync; add commands.Remove(item) in ClickyBrowserBridge.ExpirePeers() at line 2794; cap denied with FIFO eviction; and replace _003CSplitWords_003Ed__30 with a standard yield return loop.

findings.title: Synchronous analyzeScreenLayout (1280x720 JPEG Decode + Grid Scan) Blocks the Node.js Event Loop for 1.4–5.5 Seconds per Image Turn, Causing 6 Soak Test Turn Failures, Missing Answer-Line Detection, and Report-vs-PERF_DATA Drift
findings.component: Backend Screen Layout Analyzer & WS-M Benchmark Suite (`screenLayout.ts`, `brain.ts`, `PERF_DATA.json`, `REPORT.md`)
findings.description: Cross-auditing docs/audit/ws-lm/PERF_DATA.json against docs/audit/ws-lm/REPORT.md and src/backend/src/utils/screenLayout.ts revealed three important performance and measurement issues: (1) Main-thread event-loop starvation: analyzeScreenLayout (called synchronously on the main Node.js thread in brain.ts:346 on every turn containing a screenshot) decodes the 1280x720 JPEG via pure-JS jpeg-js and runs multi-pass pixel scans synchronously, blocking the entire Node.js event loop for 1,441.30 ms to 5,497.43 ms (p50 = 3,131.54 ms, p95 = 5,497.43 ms in PERF_DATA.json:140-152). During the 215-turn soak test (concurrency = 10, with 1280x720 screenshots on every 10th turn), this synchronous event-loop block caused 6 turn failures (turnErrors: 6 in PERF_DATA.json:160, p95 = 5,552.44 ms, max = 7,678.57 ms). (2) Answer-line detector misses 1px horizontal lines: Although buildSynthetic1280x720JpegDataUrl (test-perf-reliability.ts:111-116) draws three 400px-wide horizontal answer lines at y = 480, 530, 580, analyzeScreenLayout returned detectedAnswerLines: 0 (PERF_DATA.json:151) because JPEG 80% chroma/luma ringing softens 1px single-row strokes below the detector's contrast threshold. (3) Report-vs-PERF_DATA drift & PCM check bug: REPORT.md (§3.2-3.4) cites numbers from an earlier run (coldStart p50 = 556.98 ms, analyzeScreenLayout p50 = 651.12 ms, soak turnErrors = 0, SQLite growth ~49 KB -> >1.35 MB, and 'returned valid RIFF WAV speech audio'), whereas the final committed PERF_DATA.json recorded coldStart p50 = 826.28 ms (max 10,993.96 ms), analyzeScreenLayout p50 = 3,131.54 ms, soak turnErrors = 6, SQLite growth 457 KB -> 5.54 MB (+5.08 MB), and recoveredWithRealSpeechWav: false (because test-perf-reliability.ts:1114 checks for a 'RIFF' WAV header on /agent/realtime/speak, which actually returns raw headerless 24 kHz 16-bit mono PCM).
reproductionSteps:
1. Compare docs/audit/ws-lm/PERF_DATA.json lines 3-18, 140-170, 238-242, and 265 against docs/audit/ws-lm/REPORT.md lines 86-113.
2. Inspect tests/audit/ws-lm/test-perf-reliability.ts lines 111-116 and 1112-1114.
findings.observedResult: Synchronous analyzeScreenLayout blocks the event loop for 1.4–5.5s per 1280x720 screenshot turn (causing 6 soak errors under concurrency=10), misses 1px JPEG-compressed answer lines (detectedAnswerLines: 0), and PERF_DATA.json:265 reports recoveredWithRealSpeechWav: false due to checking for 'RIFF' on a raw PCM endpoint.
findings.expectedResult: analyzeScreenLayout should run off the main event loop (e.g., in a Node worker_threads pool) or downsample/short-circuit so image turns do not stall concurrent HTTP requests for 1.4–5.5s; PERF_REPORT.md should report both the unloaded and loaded numbers from PERF_DATA.json; and test-perf-reliability.ts:1114 should validate raw 24 kHz PCM byte length and non-zero sample variance rather than a 'RIFF' header.
findings.impact: Cross-auditing docs/audit/ws-lm/PERF_DATA.json against docs/audit/ws-lm/REPORT.md and src/backend/src/utils/screenLayout.ts revealed three important performance and measurement issues: (1) Main-thread event-loop starvation: analyzeScreenLayout (called synchronously on the main Node.js thread in brain.ts:346 on every turn containing a screenshot) decodes the 1280x720 JPEG via pure-JS jpeg-js and runs multi-pass pixel scans synchronously, blocking the entire Node.js event loop for 1,441.30 ms to 5,497.43 ms (p50 = 3,131.54 ms, p95 = 5,497.43 ms in PERF_DATA.json:140-152). During the 215-turn soak test (concurrency = 10, with 1280x720 screenshots on every 10th turn), this synchronous event-loop block caused 6 turn failures (turnErrors: 6 in PERF_DATA.json:160, p95 = 5,552.44 ms, max = 7,678.57 ms). (2) Answer-line detector misses 1px horizontal lines: Although buildSynthetic1280x720JpegDataUrl (test-perf-reliability.ts:111-116) draws three 400px-wide horizontal answer lines at y = 480, 530, 580, analyzeScreenLayout returned detectedAnswerLines: 0 (PERF_DATA.json:151) because JPEG 80% chroma/luma ringing softens 1px single-row strokes below the detector's contrast threshold. (3) Report-vs-PERF_DATA drift & PCM check bug: REPORT.md (§3.2-3.4) cites numbers from an earlier run (coldStart p50 = 556.98 ms, analyzeScreenLayout p50 = 651.12 ms, soak turnErrors = 0, SQLite growth ~49 KB -> >1.35 MB, and 'returned valid RIFF WAV speech audio'), whereas the final committed PERF_DATA.json recorded coldStart p50 = 826.28 ms (max 10,993.96 ms), analyzeScreenLayout p50 = 3,131.54 ms, soak turnErrors = 6, SQLite growth 457 KB -> 5.54 MB (+5.08 MB), and recoveredWithRealSpeechWav: false (because test-perf-reliability.ts:1114 checks for a 'RIFF' WAV header on /agent/realtime/speak, which actually returns raw headerless 24 kHz 16-bit mono PCM).
findings.remediation: Offload analyzeScreenLayout to a worker_threads worker with a 500 ms timeout; relax vertical stroke thickness tolerance in screenLayout.ts for JPEG-compressed 1px lines; and reconcile both unloaded and loaded PERF_DATA.json metrics in docs/audit/PERF_REPORT.md.

findings.title: README.md falsely claims setup-kursor.cmd writes session.json (actual: DPAPI auth.localdev.bin / auth.bin) and documents non-existent writeOnPage drawing primitive
findings.description:
Two technical claims in `README.md` contradict the actual codebase:
1. **`session.json` vs `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin` (`README.md:133`)**: `README.md:133` states that `setup-kursor.cmd` "Configures `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\endpoints.json` & `session.json`". In reality, `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:83-88` encrypts the local session blob with Windows DPAPI (`[System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Protect(..., CurrentUser)`) and writes `auth.localdev.bin` and `auth.bin` — never `session.json` (because `AuthStorage.cs` in `Kursor.Core` reads DPAPI-encrypted `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin`).
2. **`openPage` + `writeOnPage` claim (`README.md:20-21`)**: `README.md:20-21` lists `openPage` + `writeOnPage` under "Floating Rich-Text Cards" that "Spawn draggable, expandable on-screen study cards with markdown headings, bullet lists, and explanations". In reality, `writeOnPage` does not exist anywhere in `Assets/Engine/*.js` or `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts`, and `openPage("https://...")` (`brain.ts:106`) is the function to open a web URL in the user's browser; floating rich-text cards are actually drawn via `receipt()`, `clipping()`, `paper()`, and `sticky()`.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
findings.observedResult: `writeOnPage` has 0 occurrences in the codebase; `seed-local-auth.ps1` writes `auth.localdev.bin` and `auth.bin`, not `session.json`.
findings.expectedResult: `README.md` should accurately reference `receipt` / `clipping` / `paper` / `sticky` for floating cards and `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin` for DPAPI session files.
findings.impact:
Two technical claims in `README.md` contradict the actual codebase:
1. **`session.json` vs `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin` (`README.md:133`)**: `README.md:133` states that `setup-kursor.cmd` "Configures `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClicky\endpoints.json` & `session.json`". In reality, `scripts/seed-local-auth.ps1:83-88` encrypts the local session blob with Windows DPAPI (`[System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Protect(..., CurrentUser)`) and writes `auth.localdev.bin` and `auth.bin` — never `session.json` (because `AuthStorage.cs` in `Kursor.Core` reads DPAPI-encrypted `auth.localdev.bin` / `auth.bin`).
2. **`openPage` + `writeOnPage` claim (`README.md:20-21`)**: `README.md:20-21` lists `openPage` + `writeOnPage` under "Floating Rich-Text Cards" that "Spawn draggable, expandable on-screen study cards with markdown headings, bullet lists, and explanations". In reality, `writeOnPage` does not exist anywhere in `Assets/Engine/*.js` or `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts`, and `openPage("https://...")` (`brain.ts:106`) is the function to open a web URL in the user's browser; floating rich-text cards are actually drawn via `receipt()`, `clipping()`, `paper()`, and `sticky()`.
findings.remediation: Update `README.md:20-21` to reference `receipt`, `clipping`, `paper`, and `sticky`, and update `README.md:133` to reference `endpoints.json`, `auth.localdev.bin`, and `auth.bin`.

findings.title: docs/01-architecture-overview.md cites wrong paths/byte sizes and non-existent assets, while docs/07-kursor-roadmap.md marks unimplemented rebranding & packaging items as COMPLETED
findings.description:
Two core architectural documents contain inaccurate inventory and status claims:
1. **`docs/01-architecture-overview.md:155-177`**:
   - Claims the 5 V8 JS files (`clicky-three.js`, `clicky-three-parts.js`, `clicky-draw-engine.js`, `clicky-draw-pieces.js`, `clicky-draw-native.js`) are inside `BundledResources\` with sizes `781,132 B`, `64,849 B`, `110,937 B`, `84,965 B`, and `23,372 B`. In reality, they are inside `Assets\Engine\` with sizes `429,525 B`, `41,390 B`, `259,913 B`, `66,086 B` (`66,985 B` patched), and `50,405 B` (`docs/audit/evidence/ws-ab/js-assets-comparison.json`).
   - Claims `BundledResources\ClickyBrowserExtensionID.txt` (`34 B`) exists (it does not exist anywhere in `dist/kursor-desktop/` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HeyClickyApp\current`).
   - Claims `Assets\Clicky\*.png` (68 files), `Assets\Squad\*.png` (16 files), `Assets\StarterCards\*.png` (12 files), `Assets\ToolkitLogos\*.png` (15 files), and `Assets\Fonts\PlusJakartaSans-*.ttf` exist. reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.

findings.title: Pass 1 AUD-N-001 missed that EARS_PRIMARY_PROVIDER, MOUTH_PRIMARY_PROVIDER, and DICTATION_CLEANUP_PROVIDER in .env.example are partially/completely unwired in voice.ts, and start-kursor.ps1 sets unread HEYCLICKY_SUPABASE_URL / HEYCLICKY_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

findings.title: Missing Request Body Size Limits and Silent Swallowing of Malformed JSON Across 25+ POST/PUT Endpoints
location: src/backend/src/index.ts:19-20, src/backend/src/routes/auth.ts:184, src/backend/src/routes/worker.ts:210, src/backend/src/routes/voice.ts:13, src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts:1180, src/backend/src/routes/agents.ts:197
findings.description: The Hono server does not mount a `bodyLimit` middleware (`src/backend/src/index.ts:19-20`), allowing arbitrarily large request bodies on endpoints like `POST /memory`, `PUT /memory`, and `POST /brain/turn`. In addition, 25+ POST/PUT handlers wrap `await c.req.json()` in `try { ... } catch { // Ignore }` and proceed with an empty `{}` object instead of returning `400 Bad Request` when the client sends malformed JSON (`{"broken_json": true, `) with `Content-Type: application/json`.
reproductionSteps: Send `POST` or `PUT` requests with `Content-Type: application/json` and invalid JSON body `'{"broken_json": true, '` to all POST/PUT routes.
Inspect the HTTP status codes in `docs/audit/evidence/ws-c/route-test-matrix.json`.
findings.observedResult: The Hono server does not mount a `bodyLimit` middleware (`src/backend/src/index.ts:19-20`), allowing arbitrarily large request bodies on endpoints like `POST /memory`, `PUT /memory`, and `POST /brain/turn`. In addition, 25+ POST/PUT handlers wrap `await c.req.json()` in `try { ... } catch { // Ignore }` and proceed with an empty `{}` object instead of returning `400 Bad Request` when the client sends malformed JSON (`{"broken_json": true, `) with `Content-Type: application/json`.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Masks client serialization bugs by returning `200 OK` on corrupt JSON requests, and permits memory/disk exhaustion via oversized `PUT /memory` payloads.
findings.remediation: Add Hono `bodyLimit` middleware in `src/backend/src/index.ts` and distinguish between an intentionally empty body (`Content-Length: 0`) and malformed JSON (`SyntaxError` -> HTTP 400).

findings.title: Screenshot Reference Deduplication Protocol (clicky_file / screenshot_file / 409 screenshot_files_unavailable) Is Unimplemented in POST /brain/turn
findings.component: OneBrain Screenshot Reference Protocol (brain.ts vs BrainSession.cs / BrainClient.cs)
findings.description: `BrainSession.cs` and `BrainClient.cs` implement a screenshot-by-reference protocol to avoid re-uploading up to 32 full base64 screenshots on every turn: the worker returns `screenshot_file` in `done` (`BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:118`), `BrainSession.ThreadForWorker` (`lines 1097-1126`) replaces `image_url` with `{"type": "input_image", "clicky_file": "..."}` on subsequent turns, and if a referenced `clicky_file` is missing on the worker, the worker returns HTTP 409 or SSE error `screenshot_files_unavailable` (`BrainClient.cs:77, 174`) so the client falls back to sending full `image_url` payloads. `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts` never emits `screenshot_file` in `done` (`lines 1131-1147`) and `extractPromptInput` (`lines 318-378`) silently ignores `input_image` blocks that contain `clicky_file` without `image_url` instead of returning `409 screenshot_files_unavailable`.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `BrainSession.ThreadForWorker` (`BrainSession.cs:1097-1126`) and `BrainClient.StreamTurnAsync` (`BrainClient.cs:77-80`).
Send a `POST /brain/turn` request containing `{"type": "input_image", "clicky_file": "scr_missing_01"}` in `thread` and inspect `extractPromptInput` (`brain.ts:318-378`).
findings.observedResult: `BrainSession.cs` and `BrainClient.cs` implement a screenshot-by-reference protocol to avoid re-uploading up to 32 full base64 screenshots on every turn: the worker returns `screenshot_file` in `done` (`BrainReplyAccumulator.cs:118`), `BrainSession.ThreadForWorker` (`lines 1097-1126`) replaces `image_url` with `{"type": "input_image", "clicky_file": "..."}` on subsequent turns, and if a referenced `clicky_file` is missing on the worker, the worker returns HTTP 409 or SSE error `screenshot_files_unavailable` (`BrainClient.cs:77, 174`) so the client falls back to sending full `image_url` payloads. `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts` never emits `screenshot_file` in `done` (`lines 1131-1147`) and `extractPromptInput` (`lines 318-378`) silently ignores `input_image` blocks that contain `clicky_file` without `image_url` instead of returning `409 screenshot_files_unavailable`.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Multi-turn sessions re-upload up to 32 full base64 screenshots on every turn, and any `clicky_file`-only thread item is silently dropped instead of triggering the client's 409 fallback retry.
findings.remediation: Implement an in-memory/disk screenshot cache keyed by `screenshot_file` in `src/backend/src/routes/brain.ts`, return `screenshot_file` in the `done` SSE event, and return HTTP 409 `screenshot_files_unavailable` when an unknown `clicky_file` is encountered.

findings.title: Clipboard Snapshot Drops Handle-Based Image Formats (CF_BITMAP / CF_ENHMETAFILE) and RestoreClipboard Re-Publishes Old Content Without Transient History Markers
findings.description:
Before pasting dictated text via Ctrl+V, TextInsertion.PasteTextVerifyingLandingAsync calls SnapshotClipboard() (lines 341-395) and later RestoreClipboard(snapshot) (lines 397-430):
1. Handle formats skipped: IsHandleFormat (lines 432-437) returns true for CF_BITMAP (2), CF_METAFILEPICT (3), CF_PALETTE (9), and CF_ENHMETAFILE (14), causing SnapshotClipboard to skip them. While Windows synthesizes CF_DIB (8) when reading, once SetClipboardTextWithRetry calls EmptyClipboard(), if the original clipboard owner only placed CF_BITMAP or CF_ENHMETAFILE (or if an app expects CF_BITMAP/PNG handle formats), those formats are lost or degraded.
2. Forced delayed rendering up to 64 MB per format: Calling GetClipboardData(format) inside SnapshotClipboard (line 367) forces the source application (e.g. Excel, Photoshop, or a remote desktop session using delayed rendering) to synchronously render every advertised format up to 64 MB (line 374) on the UI/clipboard thread before dictation can paste.

RestoreClipboard pollutes Clipboard History: RestoreClipboard (lines 397-430) re-populates the old formats without setting ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing or CanIncludeInClipboardHistory = 0, causing clipboard managers and Windows Clipboard History to see a duplicate clipboard write event after every dictation.

findings.title: `OverlayWindow.ShowInScreenRecordings` property setter fires and forgets `ApplyCapturePolicyToAllAsync()` without observing exceptions
findings.description: In `OverlayWindow.cs:94`, the static property setter `ShowInScreenRecordings` invokes `ApplyCapturePolicyToAllAsync();` without awaiting the returned `Task` or attaching an exception continuation. Moreover, callers such as `LessonVideoRecorder.Start` (`LessonVideoRecorder.cs:64`) set `OverlayWindow.ShowInScreenRecordings = true` and immediately assume `SetWindowDisplayAffinity` has been updated on all overlay HWNDs, even though `ApplyCapturePolicyToAllAsync` marshals asynchronously via `DispatcherQueue.EnqueueAsync` when called off the UI thread.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `OverlayWindow.cs:86-97` and `LessonVideoRecorder.cs:64-65`.

findings.title: PhotoLoader.IsPublic IPv6 SSRF Filter Bypass (Missing NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001::/32, and ::ffff:0:0/96) and Unreachable Decompiler Artifact
findings.description: PhotoLoader.FetchByHttpAsync resolves DNS hostnames and filters each IP through PhotoLoader.IsPublic(IPAddress) (lines 557-589) to prevent LLM-generated photo() calls from fetching internal/loopback resources. While IsPublic handles IPv4 private/loopback ranges and IPv6 loopback/link-local/site-local/ULA (fc00::/7) and IsIPv4MappedToIPv6, it does not block IPv6unspecified (::), IPv6 documentation/benchmarking ranges (2001:db8::/32), or IPv6 transition prefixes that embed loopback/private IPv4 addresses (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001:0000::/32). Additionally, lines 524-526 contain unreachable decompiler artifact code (IL_042f: byte[] result3; return result3;) that triggers CS0162/CS0164 when warnings are unmasked.
reproductionSteps:
1. Inspect src/desktop/Kursor.Drawing/HeyClicky.Drawing.Media/PhotoLoader.cs lines 524-526 and 557-589.
2. Trace IsPublic(IPAddress.Parse("64:ff9b::127.0.0.1")) or IsPublic(IPAddress.IPv6Any): bytes[0] is 0x00 or 0x64, none of the IPv6 checks match, and IsPublic returns true.
findings.observedResult: IPv6 transition/unspecified/multicast addresses return true from IsPublic(), and dead label IL_042f remains at lines 524-526.
findings.expectedResult: IsPublic should reject IPAddress.IPv6Any (::), multicast (ff00::/8), NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), and Teredo (2001::/32), and dead label IL_042f should be removed.
findings.impact: PhotoLoader.FetchByHttpAsync resolves DNS hostnames and filters each IP through PhotoLoader.IsPublic(IPAddress) (lines 557-589) to prevent LLM-generated photo() calls from fetching internal/loopback resources. While IsPublic handles IPv4 private/loopback ranges and IPv6 loopback/link-local/site-local/ULA (fc00::/7) and IsIPv4MappedToIPv6, it does not block IPv6unspecified (::), IPv6 documentation/benchmarking ranges (2001:db8::/32), or IPv6 transition prefixes that embed loopback/private IPv4 addresses (NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001:0000::/32). Additionally, lines 524-526 contain unreachable decompiler artifact code (IL_042f: byte[] result3; return result3;) that triggers CS0162/CS0164 when warnings are unmasked.
findings.remediation: Reject IPAddress.IPv6Any, address.IsIPv6Multicast, and transition prefixes (0x2001/0x0000, 0x2002, 0x0064/0xff9b) in PhotoLoader.IsPublic, and delete lines 524-526.

findings.title: `ClickyThreeKernel` permanently caches failed recipe keys in an unbounded `failed` HashSet and never recovers from `loadFailed`
findings.description: `ClickyThreeKernel` (`ClickyThreeKernel.cs:30`) maintains a `HashSet<string> failed = new HashSet<string>()` of failed `"kind:recipeJson"` keys. While successful geometries in `shapes` are capped at `MaxCachedShapes = 256` with FIFO eviction (`CacheShape`, lines 142-158), `failed` has no size cap or eviction policy, and is never cleared even when the V8 runtime idles out after 300 seconds (`Run`, lines 179-190). Additionally, if `LoadEngine()` fails once (`loadFailed = true`, line 222), the kernel is permanently bricked for the lifetime of the process.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `ClickyThreeKernel.cs:30,118-158,179-240`.
findings.observedResult: `ClickyThreeKernel` (`ClickyThreeKernel.cs:30`) maintains a `HashSet<string> failed = new HashSet<string>()` of failed `"kind:recipeJson"` keys. While successful geometries in `shapes` are capped at `MaxCachedShapes = 256` with FIFO eviction (`CacheShape`, lines 142-158), `failed` has no size cap or eviction policy, and is never cleared even when the V8 runtime idles out after 300 seconds (`Run`, lines 179-190). Additionally, if `LoadEngine()` fails once (`loadFailed = true`, line 222), the kernel is permanently bricked for the lifetime of the process.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: Unbounded memory growth in `failed` over long sessions with malformed LLM recipes, and permanent blacklisting of recipes after any transient V8 error.
findings.remediation: Clear `failed` when disposing the idle V8 engine in `Run()` and cap `failed.Count` to `256` entries in `MarkFailed()`.

findings.title: `Pipelines.Shared` permanently disables all 3D rendering (`buildFailed = true`) on any transient shader/pipeline error and `GpuDevice.Shared` cannot recover from device loss
findings.description: `GpuDevice.Shared` (`GpuDevice.cs:19`) is a static `Lazy<GpuDevice>` singleton with no mechanism to recreate the `ID3D11Device` or `ID2D1Device` if `GetDeviceRemovedReason()` becomes non-zero. Furthermore, `Pipelines.Shared` (`Pipelines.cs:145-165`) catches any exception during pipeline construction, sets a static `buildFailed = true`, and returns `null` for the remainder of the process lifetime.
reproductionSteps: Inspect `GpuDevice.cs:19-45` and `Pipelines.cs:20,145-165`.
findings.observedResult: `GpuDevice.Shared` (`GpuDevice.cs:19`) is a static `Lazy<GpuDevice>` singleton with no mechanism to recreate the `ID3D11Device` or `ID2D1Device` if `GetDeviceRemovedReason()` becomes non-zero. Furthermore, `Pipelines.Shared` (`Pipelines.cs:145-165`) catches any exception during pipeline construction, sets a static `buildFailed = true`, and returns `null` for the remainder of the process lifetime.
findings.expectedResult: Component should adhere to API contract, security boundary, and specification without error.
findings.impact: If the D3D11 device is removed or reset, all 3D stages (`ThreeStage.FrameLoop`) catch the exception, set `paused = true` (`ThreeStage.cs:1347`), and 3D rendering ceases until the application is restarted.
findings.remediation: Replace the immutable `Lazy<GpuDevice>` singleton with a resettable device manager that recreates `GpuDevice` and `Pipelines` when `ID3D11Device.GetDeviceRemovedReason()` indicates device removal.

findings.title: EarconPlayer.DecodeWavToStereo48k Throws DivideByZeroException on Sub-8-Bit WAV and PermissionService Leaks RegistryKey
findings.description: 1) EarconPlayer.DecodeWavToStereo48k computes int num5 = Math.Max(1, num2) * (bitsPerSample / 8) and int num6 = num4 / num5 without validating bitsPerSample >= 8 or num > 0. findings.title: ClickyInkPatchStream.PartialText Rejects Unified Diff Hunk Headers (@@ ... @@) and Strips First Character of Unprefixed Context Lines
findings.description: ClickyInkPatchStream.PartialText (lines 49-67) extracts text3 = text2.Substring(2).TrimWs() from every '@@' header and searches for a document line literally matching text3 via Same(list[k], text3). If an LLM emits a standard unified diff header ('@@ -2,1 +2,2 @@') or a V4A header with a trailing '@@' ('@@ Heading @@'), text3 never matches any line in list and PartialText returns null (as observed in WsHiAuditRunner Suite 3 where 'patched length=-1'). Additionally, line 80 strips the first character of every non-'+' line via l.Substring(1) without checking whether the line starts with ' ' or '-'.

findings.title: Inaccurate C# file counts across README.md (2,102), AGENTS.md (2,098), docs/INDEX.md, docs/06, and docs/07 vs actual repository file counts (2,096 and 2,097)
findings.description:
Every documentation file that cites C# file counts is off by 1 to 5 files (`docs/audit/evidence/ws-ab/docs-audit.json`):
- **`reference/decompiled/`**: `AGENTS.md:14`, `docs/INDEX.md:24-34`, `docs/06:6`, and `docs/07:100` claim **2,098 `.cs` files** (`56 + 565 + 123 + 86 + 42 + 346 + 880`). The actual `.cs` file count in `reference/decompiled/` is **2,096 `.cs` files** (`55 + 564 + 122 + 85 + 41 + 345 + 884`) because the original author counted all files in each folder including the `.csproj` file in 6 projects (`+6`) while miscounting `HeyClicky.App` (`880` vs `884`).
- **`src/desktop/`**: `README.md:3`, `docs/INDEX.md:55-62`, and `docs/07:31` claim **2,102 C# files** (`56 + 42 + 86 + 346 + 565 + 123 + 884`). The actual `.cs` file count in `src/desktop/` is **2,097 `.cs` files** (`55 + 41 + 85 + 345 + 564 + 122 + 884 = 2,096` across the 7 project folders, plus `1` root file `src/desktop/PrivateImplementationDetailsPolyfill.cs`).
- Note: Backend test counts in `docs/INDEX.md:40,51` (`18/18` in `test-phase1.ts` + `7/7` in `test-phase2.ts` = `25/25`) match actual `testEndpoint(...)` invocations.
reproductionSteps: See workstream audit test suite and evidence.
